Title: Three 15-year-olds plead guilty to beating classmate over WhatsApp messages
Article:
TANGKAK: Three 15-year-old students pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court today to assaulting a classmate in a bullying incident at a secondary school in Taman Sri Kesang.
The three entered their pleas before magistrate Arthana Sarma Rao after the charge was read out.
They were jointly charged with voluntarily causing hurt to their 15-year-old classmate by punching and kicking him.
The offence was allegedly committed at the school between 8am and 11.30am on Nov 13.

Title: National Laureate A. Samad Said laid to rest at Bukit Kiara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said was laid to rest at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery here at 10.55am today.
Earlier, more than 300 people, including family members, fellow arts practitioners and members of the public, performed funeral prayers at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar, led by the mosque's chief imam, Muhammad Abid Ayub.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and veteran newsman Datuk A. Kadir Jasin.
Among those who paid their last respects at the cemetery were DAP veteran Tan Sri Lim Kit Siang, OKU Sentral president Datuk Dr Ras Adiba Mohd Radzi and three National Laureates – Datuk Dr Anwar Ridhwan, Prof Datuk Dr Siti Zainon Ismail and Datuk Dr Zurinah Hassan.
Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) director-general Datuk Dr Hazami Jahari and singer and composer Datuk M. Nasir were also present.
A. Samad died at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment for diabetes and age-related ailments at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL). He was 91.
Born on April 9, 1935, in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, A. Samad was named the country's fourth National Laureate in 1985.
He was renowned for literary masterpieces including the novels Salina, Sungai Mengalir Lesu and Hujan Pagi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alliance Bank posts marginal Q2 earnings growth, raises dividend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's net profit rose 0.93 per cent to RM208.47 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM206.56 million a year ago, as revenue increased 3.56 per cent to RM648.50 million from RM626.23 million.
For the first half, net profit increased 12.71 per cent to RM456.78 million from RM405.26 million a year ago, while revenue grew 3.05 per cent to RM1.28 billion from RM1.24 billion.
The bank proposed an interim dividend of 11.88 sen per share for the financial year ending March 31, 2027, up from 9.37 sen a year earlier.
Alliance Bank said its first-half performance was supported by higher net interest income, stronger client-based fee income and lower net credit costs.
The bank continued to prioritise asset quality over loan growth, increasing its exposure to secured consumer financing and business lending while scaling back unsecured consumer lending to strengthen its portfolio and improve risk-adjusted returns.
Its total assets expanded 13 per cent year-on-year to RM97.70 billion.
Group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the results reflected the momentum of the bank's Acceler8 strategy and its focus on disciplined growth and portfolio quality.
"Entering the final stretch of Acceler8 2027 with strong capital and liquidity buffers, we remain focused on investing in technology, data, artificial intelligence capabilities and our people.
"We also continue to support our customers through global uncertainties and deliver sustainable long-term value to all our stakeholders," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher acquitted in RM65k forged salary slip case
Article:
KOTA BARU: A teacher was acquitted and discharged by the Sessions Court today over an amended charge of fraudulently using a forged salary slip to obtain a RM65,000 loan six years ago.
Judge Dazuki Ali ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case.
The 48-year-old teacher, Norzaiza Ab Rahman, was accused of using a purportedly genuine December 2019 salary slip issued by the Accountant General's Department of Malaysia in Kelantan to apply for the loan.
According to the amended charge, she allegedly committed the offence at Bank Simpanan Nasional in Jalan Pintu Pong, here, between Jan 12 and 14, 2020.
She was charged under Section 471 of the Penal Code, which is punishable under Section 465 of the same code.
Lawyer Muhammad Hasif Hasan represented Norzaiza, while Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Asmah Che Wan appeared for the prosecution in Kelantan.
Speaking after the decision, Hasif said his client, who has three children, was relieved and grateful that the six-year legal battle had finally come to an end.
He said the case had taken a heavy toll on her life and caused considerable distress over the years.
"Today's decision clearly shows that my client is not guilty. It also clears her name in the eyes of the public and allows her to move forward with her career," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five killed in military helicopter crash in Turkiye
Article:
ANKARA: Five Turkish Air Force personnel were killed when an AS-532 military helicopter crashed during a training flight in Eskisehir province, central Turkiye, on Tuesday, according to Turkish broadcaster NTV, reported Xinhua.
Citing a statement from the Turkish Defence Ministry, NTV said the wreckage had been located and search and rescue operations were under way.
Firefighters from the Eskisehir Metropolitan Municipality had also arrived at the site to assist in the search and rescue efforts, it added.

Title: Malaysia's leading index rises 2.2pct in September, signals positive outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index (LI) rose 2.2 per cent year-on-year to 116.0 points in September 2026 from 113.5 points in the same month last year.
The Statistics Department said the growth was mainly driven by a 44.1 per cent increase in real imports of basic precious and other non-ferrous metals, alongside an 11.5 per cent rise in real imports of semiconductors.
"However, this increase was partly offset by declines in several other components, particularly the number of housing units approved," it said.
On a month-on-month basis, the LI fell 0.3 per cent, mainly weighed down by lower expected manufacturing sales value.
The department said the LI remained above its long-term trend of 100.0 points in September, indicating a positive economic outlook in the coming months.
"This positive outlook is expected to continue being driven by encouraging export performance, domestic sector resilience, and sustained strategic investment inflows.
"Nevertheless, geopolitical developments and the uncertain global trade landscape warrant close monitoring," it added.
Meanwhile, the coincident index (CI), which measures current economic performance, increased 2.5 per cent year-on-year to 132.4 points in September from 129.2 points a year earlier.
The increase was supported by growth across all components, particularly the industrial production index and real contributions to the Employees Provident Fund, which rose 6.3 per cent and 5.8 per cent, respectively.
On a monthly basis, the CI increased 0.8 per cent, driven by manufacturing capacity utilisation and the volume index of retail trade.

Title: Anwar yet to accept Loke's resignation, says he is still on leave
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to accept Anthony Loke's resignation as Transport Minister, saying the latter is still on leave.
Anwar confirmed that he had met Loke to discuss the matter.
"I have not accepted the resignation; he is still on leave," he said when asked about Loke's cabinet status at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.

Title: Warisan calls for clearer welfare support for medical officers sent to Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry should clarify accommodation, allowances and other welfare arrangements for medical officers deployed to Sabah to address the state's shortage of healthcare personnel, said Dr Istefan Koh.
The Parti Warisan Health Bureau spokesperson said clear arrangements are needed to ensure doctors from Peninsular Malaysia are adequately supported during their deployment.
Sabah is facing a shortage of 245 medical officers following the second phase of a permanent appointment exercise involving the transfer of doctors, according to a report earlier this month.
The Sabah Health Department said the transferred doctors were supposed to be replaced, but 67 per cent of replacement candidates from outside the state failed to report for duty despite accepting permanent appointments.
Koh said several aspects of the deployment arrangements required clarification, particularly accommodation and allowances.
"One of the main matters that needs clarification is accommodation.
"Will the Sabah Health Department provide accommodation throughout the deployment period? If so, will it be free of charge, or will medical officers have to bear the cost themselves?
"Will officers instructed to serve outside their usual stations or states receive appropriate allowances?
"What about meal, transport and accommodation allowances? Will return flight tickets be fully covered by the government, or will officers have to pay upfront before submitting claims?" he said in a statement.
He said the ministry should also clarify how long officers would have to wait for reimbursement if they were required to pay the expenses upfront and claim them later.
Koh said responsibility for providing facilities and safeguarding the welfare of deployed officers should not rest solely with the federal government.
He said the Sabah government should work with the federal government to provide additional incentives, financial assistance and accommodation for doctors from Peninsular Malaysia serving in the state.
"The people of Sabah themselves are bearing the consequences of the shortage of medical personnel.
"Therefore, the state government must step forward as a strategic partner to ensure continued access to healthcare services."
As a temporary measure, he said the state government could consider allocating special funds for additional allowances, cost-of-living assistance, accommodation and basic facilities for medical officers from Peninsular Malaysia who accepted temporary placements in Sabah.
In the longer term, Koh said the Sabah government should invest more in developing local healthcare talent.
"Efforts to increase the number of Sabahans given opportunities to pursue medical studies must be strengthened through scholarships, educational assistance and partnerships with higher education institutions.
"At the same time, opportunities for specialist training and career development for local doctors must be expanded so that more Sabah medical graduates can return to serve and build their careers in their home state."

Title: UMS gets approval to increase annual medical student intake to 150
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Higher Education Ministry has approved an annual intake of up to 150 medical students at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS).
Its vice-chancellor, Professor Dr Rosalam Sarbatly, said UMS would increase enrolment in phases in line with its clinical training capacity.
He said the phased approach would ensure every student received adequate training placements, supervision and opportunities to learn alongside patients across all major disciplines.
"As an initial step, UMS has increased its annual intake from 90 to 100 students," he said in a statement.
Rosalam said the university would continue working with the Health Ministry (MOH), through the Sabah State Health Department, to coordinate student placements and supervision at government hospitals and clinics.
He said UMS Hospital was also expanding its services as a teaching hospital in phases, which would provide additional clinical training placements once fully operational.
UMS currently offers specialist training in public health medicine, emergency medicine and anaesthesiology, he said, while programmes in rehabilitation medicine, orthopaedics and family medicine were in the final stages of development.
"My aspiration is for more Sabahans to have the opportunity to study medicine and pursue specialist training in their home state, before going on to serve the people of Sabah," he said.
On the Sabah government's announcement of
special scholarships
for local medical students at UMS, Rosalam said the aid would ease their financial burden and support the Sabah Maju Jaya 2.0 agenda to train more doctors for the state's healthcare needs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Proton bids farewell to Persona after 19 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Proton's Persona sedan has reached the end of the road after 19 years in production, with the final unit handed over to a customer at its 4S dealership, Atiara Johan, in Puchong.
The model, introduced on Aug 15, 2007, recorded cumulative sales of 473,346 units across domestic and export markets, making it one of the national carmaker's key sedan models.
The Persona succeeded the Proton Wira and was developed using the Proton Gen-2 platform.
"A new generation arrived on Aug 23, 2016, drawing on the Proton Iriz platform and introducing further improvements in safety, refinement and practicality.
"Subsequent updates in 2019 and 2021 kept the model relevant as customer expectations evolved," Proton said in a statement.
Proton Edar sales director Ong Chee Wooi said the Persona had served Malaysian households by offering an affordable sedan with space, comfort and practicality.
"We recognise the customers who placed their trust in the Persona and everyone who contributed to its success.
"Its significance lies in the opportunities it created for Malaysians to own a car that met their needs, supported their livelihoods and became part of their family stories," he added.
The Persona has been superseded by the Proton S70 1.5 i-GT, which is available in Lite and Prime variants.
Both variants are powered by a naturally aspirated 1.5-litre i-GT engine paired with a continuously variable transmission.
The S70 1.5 i-GT also comes with six airbags, a reverse camera, a rear seat reminder, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, as well as an electric parking brake with Auto Brake Hold.
Prices start at RM56,800 on the road without insurance, after a RM3,000 early bird rebate, subject to terms and conditions. The starting price before the rebate is RM59,800.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Police: RMAF pilot in RM4.83mil drug haul acted as coordinator, transporter
Article:
TUMPAT: A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) pilot arrested in connection with the seizure of 96.6kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million at the Subang Airbase was a coordinator and transporter for the drug syndicate.
Bukit Aman confirmed that the pilot was among 13 people arrested over the seizure.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations were ongoing, including into the payments received by the suspects.
Preliminary investigations found that the syndicate transported drugs from Subang to Labuan and Tawau, Sabah, although other destinations had not been ruled out.
"Each member of a syndicate has a specific role. The 13 arrested so far are believed to be part of the syndicate.
"The pilot acted as a coordinator and transporter, moving drug supplies from the Klang Valley to Sabah," he said.
Hussein said the amount paid to the pilot was still under investigation and could not be disclosed.
Hussein was speaking to reporters during a visit to the family of Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, who died in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, on Nov 17.
He said police had identified several syndicate members before making the arrests.
So far, 13 people have been arrested, including seven
RMAF officers
and personnel and six civilians.
"Investigations are ongoing to identify other syndicate members, and several others have been identified for further action.
"Information on the number of trips made using military assets is also still being investigated.
"Give the police time to complete the investigation. The Inspector-General of Police will share the findings later," he said.
Police had earlier confirmed the arrest of 13 people, including seven RMAF officers and personnel, following the seizure of 96.6kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million at Subang Airbase.
The six civilians arrested included two syndicate coordinators. The arrests were made in operations across the Klang Valley, Labuan and Sabah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Overseas disaster deaths require stronger international cooperation, says Saifuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs stronger cooperation with other countries to facilitate the registration of Malaysians who die in disasters overseas, the Dewan Rakyat heard today.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said existing procedures for registering ordinary deaths abroad were adequate, but disaster-related cases were more complex as they involved the legal and administrative requirements of the countries concerned.
He said Malaysia's domestic mechanisms alone were insufficient to resolve such cases without complying with the procedures of the countries where the disasters occurred.
"What we need to address are situations involving tragedies such as aircraft crashes or disasters abroad, which are slightly more complex.
"We are learning to improve our domestic processes while strengthening and refining cooperation with other countries," he said.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) whether the government planned to introduce an integrated standard operating procedure (SOP) and a fast-track documentation mechanism for Malaysians who go missing in disasters abroad.
Saifuddin said under the existing mechanism, the National Registration Department (NRD) could issue death certificates within seven working days upon receiving the necessary documentation for ordinary deaths abroad.
He said the department had also simplified certain requirements, including allowing applicants to fill in an alternative form if they could not produce the deceased's identity card.
"I believe the existing mechanism is reasonable and adequate. There are no hiccups. Seven working days is already quite fast," he said.
On the 54 Malaysians who remain missing following the Aug 26 flood tragedy in Nepal, Saifuddin said Malaysia had decided to fully comply with Nepal's legal and administrative procedures in managing declarations of presumed death.
He said Nepal had amended its laws to shorten the presumption-of-death period for disaster victims from 12 years to 45 days following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's intervention.
Saifuddin said the NRD would issue death certificates once it received confirmation from the Nepalese government.
He added that cooperation from the victims' next of kin in completing the required documentation was crucial to expediting the process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher claims trial to sexual assault charges involving 14-year-old student
Article:
SEREMBAN: A secondary school teacher in Jelebu pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to two charges involving the sexual assault of a 14-year-old Form Three student and showing him a sexual video.
Muhammad Faaris Ar-Radhi Mohamad Fadzil, 29, entered the plea before judge Ahmad Fuad Othman after the charges were read out.
On the first charge, he is accused of sexually assaulting the student, who was 14 years and eight months old at the time, while in a position of trust as his teacher.
The charge, under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 (Act 792), read together with Section 16(1), carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
On the second charge, he is accused of showing the same student a sexual video through social media using his mobile phone.
The charge, under Section 15(e) of Act 792, read together with Section 16(1), carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both.
Under Section 16, both offences also carry an additional jail term of up to five years and a minimum of two strokes of the cane.
Both offences were allegedly committed in the school's teachers' room between 10pm and 10.30pm on Aug 17, 2026.
Deputy public prosecutor Norazihah Asmuni prosecuted, while Umar Zulkarnain represented the accused.
The court set bail at RM15,000 and ordered the accused not to contact or disturb the victim, to report to a police station monthly and to surrender his passport until the case is concluded.
The case was fixed for mention on Dec 22 for the submission of documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Crocodile sighting in Klang River sparks online buzz [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A crocodile sighting in the Klang River has drawn attention after several people recorded videos of the reptile, which were later shared on social media.
One video was uploaded to Threads by a user identified as epilogkehidupan94, accompanied by a humorous caption.
"Meet Gorgon (the crocodile) of the Klang River. Whose husband is this? Come and collect him," the user wrote.
The video drew mixed reactions, with some netizens initially mistaking the reptile for an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated image.
One user, alifafiq141, pointed out that warning signs featuring crocodile images had been put up along the Klang River, from the Damansara area towards Kuala Lumpur.
"Many people think this is AI-generated. But there are warning signs along the Klang River from Damansara to Kuala Lumpur," the user wrote.
Others expressed concern over the sighting, particularly as the river is a popular fishing spot.
"I'm worried because many children fish along the Klang River embankment.
"With the December school holidays approaching, many schoolchildren are likely to come here to fish," another user, hafizbeanrahman, wrote.
A third user, ikinjer, claimed that two or three crocodiles had been spotted in the area.
"Sometimes, if you're lucky while spending time at Kika Cafe near the spot, you can see crocodiles swimming calmly," the user wrote.
Meanwhile, the Kuala Lumpur office of the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) said it had checked with the Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) but had yet to receive any public complaints about a crocodile sighting in the Klang River.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three men remanded four days over assault of 62-year-old man
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Three men have been remanded for four days from today to assist investigations into the assault of a 62-year-old man following a road accident at Lorong Ikhwan, Jalan Pasir Panjang, on Monday.
The remand order, which runs until Saturday, was issued by magistrate Muhammad Amir Zainul Muttaqin Mohd Zamri.
Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the suspects, aged between 39 and 44, were arrested yesterday afternoon.
He said the incident was believed to have started when a Perodua Alza rear-ended a Skoda driven by the victim's wife.
"When the victim stepped out to inspect the damage, he was attacked by the occupants of the Perodua Alza," he said.
The victim suffered injuries to his face, nose and mouth after being punched and elbowed by three men around 5pm.
A video of the assault later went viral on Facebook, drawing public outrage.
The case is being investigated under Section 325 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt, which carries a maximum jail term of seven years and a fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Matrix Concepts founder Lee Tian Hock named Property Man of the Year 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd founder and group executive deputy chairman Datuk Seri Lee Tian Hock has been named FIABCI Malaysia Property Man of the Year 2026.
The company's flagship development, Bandar Sri Sendayan, additionally won the Master Plan and Township category at the FIABCI Malaysia Property Award 2026.
The double recognition comes as the property developer marks its 30th anniversary this year, highlighting its growth from a Negeri Sembilan-based developer into a diversified property group with operations in the Klang Valley, Johor, Australia and Indonesia.
Lee founded Matrix Concepts in 1996, with its first development, Taman Bahau in Negeri Sembilan, launched in 1997.
The company said the award recognised his more than 40 years of experience in property development and his contribution to shaping the group's growth and standing in the industry.
Under his leadership, Matrix Concepts has expanded beyond property development into construction, education, healthcare and hospitality.
The group has also received several industry accolades, including recognition among the Top 10 Developers in the Edge Malaysia Property Excellence Awards.
Lee said the recognition reflected the collective contributions of his family, employees and business partners.
"Buildings may stand for decades, but trust can last for generations. I came from very humble beginnings, and I have never forgotten what it means to have very little.
"Whatever success we achieve should create opportunities for others to move forward. I have always believed that wealth is only meaningful when it is used to uplift others," he said.
Matrix Concepts said Lee's contributions also extended to education, scholarships, healthcare, sports development and community welfare.
The company added that it was among three property companies to have received both the FIABCI Malaysia Property CEO and Property Man honours, following the recognition of its then group managing director Ho Kong Soon as Property CEO in 2022.
Its earlier project, Hijayu 2- Resort Homes, also won the Residential Low-Rise category in 2023.
Meanwhile, Bandar Sri Sendayan's recognition in the Master Plan and Township category reflects its development into an integrated township spanning approximately 6,800 acres in Negeri Sembilan.
The township is home to more than 120,000 residents and comprises residential, commercial, educational, healthcare, hospitality and recreational facilities.
Its developments include Sendayan TechValley, commercial hubs, schools, healthcare facilities and green spaces, supporting its role as a township where residents can live, work, learn and grow.
Matrix Concepts said the township's master plan had continued to evolve alongside the needs of its growing community over more than two decades.
As the winner of the category, Bandar Sri Sendayan will have the opportunity to represent Malaysia at the FIABCI World Prix d'Excellence Awards 2027 in Toronto, Canada.
The FIABCI Malaysia Property Awards, organised by FIABCI-Malaysia, recognise excellence in property development, with winning projects eligible to compete at the international awards.
"There is still much more to be done. More homes to make possible, more communities to strengthen, more opportunities to create, and more young lives to uplift through education and sport.
My hope is that our legacy will not be measured only by the buildings bearing our name but by the lives made better because we were here," Lee added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTS Link fares to be announced in January
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Fares for the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, covering one-way and return journeys, are expected to be announced in January next year.
This is ahead of the service's scheduled launch in February 2027.
Johor public works, transport, infrastructure and communications committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the fares are still being discussed and reviewed by the relevant parties, including RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) and the Malaysian and Singapore governments.
He said the official fares had yet to be finalised, with the Transport Ministry expected to announce them in January 2027.
"The official fares for one-way and return journeys have yet to be finalised. Discussions are ongoing between the parties involved," he said during the state assembly sitting at Kota Iskandar here today.
He was responding to Baharudin Mohamed Taib (BN-Permas), who asked about the proposed fares and when they would be announced.
Mohamad Fazli said the state government recognised that fares were a major concern, particularly for Malaysians who would rely on the service for their daily commutes to Singapore.
He hoped the final rates would take into account the affordability and needs of regular commuters.
About 400,000 Malaysians are estimated to travel daily across the Johor-Singapore Causeway to work in Singapore, making affordable and reliable cross-border transport a key consideration.
He said preparations for the RTS Link's opening must also include adequate feeder bus services, seamless onward connections and improved traffic management across Greater Johor Bahru.
"The priority is to ensure people can travel more easily, systematically and safely, while enjoying more predictable journey times," he said.
The RTS Link is expected to begin operations in February 2027, following the completion of system testing and trial operations.
The 4km cross-border rail service will connect Bukit Chagar station in Johor Baru with Woodlands North station in Singapore. It is designed to carry up to 10,000 passengers an hour in each direction.
The service is expected to ease congestion at the Johor-Singapore Causeway, one of the region's busiest land crossings.
Former transport minister Anthony Loke had indicated that a one-way
RTS Link journey
could cost between RM15.50 and RM21.70.
Loke said the fares would be higher than conventional public transport rates in the Klang Valley but would remain more cost-effective than driving into Singapore.
The fares will be determined commercially by RTSO, a joint venture between Malaysia's Prasarana Malaysia Bhd and Singapore's SMRT Corporation.
Loke resigned as transport minister with immediate effect on Nov 10, following the High Court decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New Mount Kinabalu trail from Kiau to launch on Jan 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Climbers will soon enjoy a new Mount Kinabalu trail from Kampung Kiau in Kadamaian, scheduled to launch on Jan 16 next year.
Introduced as a high-potential tourism product in conjunction with Visit Sabah Year 2027, the 7km first phase of the exclusive Kiau-Marai-Parai trail connects Kampung Kiau Nuluh (977 metres) to Marai-Parai at 1,652 metres above sea level.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick said development on the Kadamaian side is a core focus of the Kadamaian Development Master Plan 2020-2035 and is expected to be a new economic catalyst for local residents.
"I appreciate Sabah Parks' (TTS) initiative in developing the area's potential, including the new trail from Kiau, Sayap Peak, Minitinduk Gorge, Mount Nungkok and plans in Melangkap.
"I am confident that developing Mount Kinabalu on the Kadamaian side will be a game changer for the local economy," the Kadamaian assemblyman said after a working visit to the TTS headquarters here yesterday.
Earlier, he was briefed on the tourism plans by TTS director Datuk Dr Maklarin Lakim.
According to TTS, a scientific expedition to Marai-Parai in October 2024 identified 25 main attractions along the route, including Minitinduk Gorge — part of Sir Hugh Low's historic 1851 ascent trail — alongside endemic flora and pitcher plant species (Nepenthes rajah, lowii and edwardsiana).
Under the overall plan, the route from Kampung Kiau Nuluh via Marai-Parai and West Gurkha Hut to Low's Peak spans 15.28 km, while the entire journey to Timpohon Gate covers about 24 km.
Ewon said sector development must be supported by strong infrastructure, including the Rural Road Project (JALB), and pledged his commitment to securing the necessary allocations.
Beyond Marai-Parai, TTS also highlighted Kadamaian's potential — encompassing Kiau, Melangkap, Sayap and Tambatuon — as a community-based ecotourism hub featuring Sayap Peak (3,050 metres), Mount Nungkok, waterfalls and local culture.
Of Kinabalu Park's total 75,370ha, 25,700ha or 34.1 per cent lie within the Kota Belud district, while 42.1 per cent are in Ranau and 23.8 per cent in Kota Marudu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOIPG Reit targets yield growth, acquisitions after RM2bil IPO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Newly listed IOI Properties Group Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG Reit) plans to enhance yields across its retail, hotel and office assets while pursuing acquisitions to strengthen income distributions to unitholders over the next three years.
IOIPG Reit Management Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Chris Chong Voon Foo said the trust would focus on improving the performance of its existing portfolio through asset enhancement initiatives, stronger hotel business development and better services for office tenants.
For its retail assets, the Reit will explore enhancement opportunities at its shopping malls to improve the tenant and shopper experience, optimise space utilisation and support rental growth.
In the hotel segment, it will seek to tap new markets and business opportunities to improve occupancy and revenue, while upgrading amenities and services at its office properties to enhance tenant satisfaction and support rental yields.
On acquisitions, Chong said the Reit would closely monitor the pipeline of properties identified by its sponsor, IOI Properties Group Bhd (IOIPG), in the prospectus.
The trust would assess potential acquisitions when the assets mature and become available, taking into account their suitability and contribution to the portfolio, he said after the Reit's listing on Bursa Malaysia today.
The Reit's initial portfolio comprises nine properties with an aggregate appraised value of about RM7.66 billion as of May 31, 2026.
Its portfolio is anchored by IOI City Mall in Putrajaya, which has a net lettable area (NLA) of over 2.5 million sq ft and a committed occupancy rate of 97.9 per cent as of May 31, 2026.
The portfolio also includes six hotels operating under Marriott International's portfolio of brands. They are Putrajaya Marriott Hotel, Le Méridien Putrajaya, Moxy Putrajaya, Four Points by Sheraton Puchong, W Kuala Lumpur and Courtyard by Marriott Penang.
The combination of retail, hospitality and office properties provides the Reit with diversified income streams, while its sponsor's asset pipeline offers potential opportunities to expand its portfolio over time.
However, the Reit made a subdued debut on Bursa Malaysia, opening at 87 sen, down four sen or 4.4 per cent from its initial public offering (IPO) price of 91 sen. About 2.15 million units changed hands at the opening bell.
The listing followed an IPO through which IOIPG raised about RM2 billion, valuing the offering at about US$486.3 million.
The listing represents Malaysia's largest Reit IPO to date.
Based on its IPO price of 91 sen and an issued fund size of 5.5 billion units, IOIPG Reit had a market capitalisation of about RM5 billion upon listing.
Despite the weaker opening, the Reit's longer-term performance will depend on its ability to grow rental and hotel income, improve asset yields and execute acquisitions while maintaining sustainable distributions to unitholder
Meanwhile, Kenanga Research said about a month ago that the Reit sector was likely to remain under pressure from higher bond yields, although much of the impact may already be reflected in valuations.
It expects performance across property segments to remain mixed, with retail occupancy easing to 77.9 per cent in the first half of 2026 from 78.9 per cent in the second half of 2025, amid cautious consumer sentiment stemming partly from tensions in the Middle East.
In contrast, office occupancy improved to 72.6 per cent from 71.9 per cent, indicating healthier domestic business activity.
The hospitality segment also experienced a softer first half, weighed down by higher airfares and geopolitical uncertainty.
However, the research firm expects a gradual recovery if tensions ease, supported by tourism allocations under the 2027 budget and its projections of 30 million tourist arrivals in Malaysia in 2026, up 11 per cent from 2025.

Title: Court issues gag order in Shuhaily assault case [WATCH]
Article:
SEPANG: The magistrate's court has issued a gag order barring parties directly involved in the criminal proceedings against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain from making public statements on the case until its disposal.
The order applies to Shuhaily's nine-member legal team, the prosecution, as well as lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin, who represent the two Special Branch policemen allegedly assaulted by Shuhaily.
Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani granted the application filed by Shuhaily's lawyers yesterday, supported by an affidavit and a certificate of urgency.
Khairatul said she made the decision after hearing the defence's submissions and examining the affidavit and its exhibits.
"The court also records that the prosecution has no objection," she said.

Title: Rubiah: Rural TVET programmes focus on local jobs, better salaries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry is tailoring its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes to meet local employment needs.
The initiative includes securing agreements with employers on salary packages and job placement conditions before recruiting trainees.
Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the move aimed to reduce the migration of rural youths to urban areas by helping them secure skilled jobs with competitive salaries closer to home.
"The ministry emphasises agreements with employers in local industries on skills requirements, placement conditions and salary packages for selected programmes before recruiting TVET trainees.
"Priority is given to collaborations with industries that offer permanent employment, salaries commensurate with skill levels, social protection and career advancement opportunities," she told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Rubiah said there were more than 300 active collaborations between TVET institutions under the ministry and industry players.
She said the ministry assessed local industry needs through its 281 TVET institutions, taking into account employment projections, skill levels, manpower requirements and salary offerings when determining courses and trainee intake.
The Social Security Organisation also supported these efforts by providing labour demand data, career guidance, employer engagement and job-matching services.
"Potential trainees can be matched with employers before completing their training to ensure a faster and more orderly placement process," she said.
Rubiah said industry players were also involved in curriculum development, equipment provision, practical training, apprenticeships, professional certification and graduate recruitment.
She added that the ministry regularly conducted local studies to ensure its TVET programmes remained relevant to changing economic and industry needs.
"We discontinue or introduce courses and modules in specific areas based on the skills required to develop a skilled workforce and create entrepreneurial opportunities.
"These adjustments are being implemented progressively nationwide as part of efforts to reduce the migration of young workers from rural to urban areas," she said.
Rubiah said the ministry's key performance indicators went beyond graduate employability to include competitiveness and the ability to earn higher incomes.

Title: Marine police foil international smuggling bid, syabu worth RM5.3mil seized, four nabbed
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Marine police foiled an international syabu smuggling attempt off Kedah, seizing narcotics and vehicles worth RM5.36 million following a high-speed chase. .
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the operation, codenamed Op Taring Gelora, was launched at 9pm on Nov 14 following intelligence that a syndicate was using a fibreglass boat to smuggle syabu to a neighbouring country.
A team comprising one officer and 18 personnel from Region One Marine Police (PPM), supported by its Marine Intelligence Unit and patrol boats PSC 45, PSC 60 and PIB 01, spotted the suspicious vessel about seven nautical miles off Pulau Sayak in Tanjung Dawai.
"When ordered to stop for inspection, the boat sped off and performed several dangerous manoeuvres to evade arrest.
"However, our team intercepted the vessel at 10.30pm after a 90-minute chase, detaining two Indonesian men on board," he told a press conference at the Region One PPM headquarters here today.
Also present were PPM commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Shamsol Kassim and Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar.
Yusri said checks revealed five white sacks containing 100 gold-coloured plastic packets labelled "VIP 666", filled with 103.798kg of syabu worth RM5,189,900.
"Follow-up intelligence the next day led police to raid a house in Kampung Sungai Layar Hujung, Sungai Petani, where they arrested a Malaysian man and another Indonesian man," he said.
He said the 36-year-old local suspect, who is self-employed and runs a grocery shop, is believed to be the mastermind, having planned and coordinated the shipment.
The suspect allegedly promised the transporters RM12,000 for each trip.
"Although the three Indonesian suspects hold valid passports, they are believed to have bypassed official entry points to operate at sea," he said.
Police also seized the fibreglass boat and a Toyota Hilux, bringing the total value of the seizures to RM5,361,400.
Yusri said the syabu was sourced locally and intended for distribution in a neighbouring country. The seizure could have supplied 518,990 drug users.
"This success deals a major blow to the syndicate's cross-border supply chain. We will not compromise with anyone attempting to turn our waters into a transit route for drug smuggling and cross-border crime," he said.
He added that police were working closely with the Kedah Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department to track down the suppliers, financiers and remaining syndicate members.
Meanwhile, Yusri said Region One PPM recorded 151 cases under the Dangerous Drugs Act from January to November this year, involving 180 arrests and seizures worth RM11.96 million.
During the same period, the unit recorded 2,375 cases, made 1,462 arrests and seized items worth more than RM187.99 million across all enforcement operations.
The four suspects, aged between 31 and 36, are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The offence carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction if the death penalty is not imposed.

Title: High Court dismisses bid to challenge diesel subsidy removal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today dismissed a bid by two men to challenge the government's decision to end blanket diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in June 2024.
Judge Datuk Norliza Othman ruled that the decision was a fiscal and economic policy matter that was not amenable to judicial review.
She also found that the government's decision to retain diesel subsidies in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan was reasonable and not arbitrary.
Norliza dismissed the application for leave to commence judicial review by Azhani Marlan @ Abd Halim and Mohd Hatta Sanuri, with RM5,000 in costs.
In her ruling, she said the exemption for Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan was based on objective considerations, including their reliance on diesel-powered vehicles due to geographical factors and road conditions.
She said removing subsidies in these states could also have a greater knock-on effect on the already higher prices of goods, while their readiness and access to information for implementing targeted subsidies had also been considered.
These factors were rationally connected to the policy's objectives and did not establish an arguable violation of Article 8 of the Federal Constitution, she said.
"The court agrees with the federal counsel's argument that the court should not interfere in social and economic matters, which fall within the government's jurisdiction and discretion to act in the interests of the people.
"Generally, if the court interferes in administrative matters undertaken by the executive, it would run contrary to the doctrine of separation of powers," she said.
However, Norliza stressed that the courts could intervene when government policies or executive actions violated the Federal Constitution or involved bad faith or abuse of power.
She found that the applicants' challenge did not fall within these exceptions.
Norliza also rejected their argument that the government had failed to follow the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula in setting diesel retail prices.
She said their calculations were unsupported by reliable documents and did not account for prevailing foreign exchange rates.
"The allegation that the government imposed a hidden charge of more than 40 sen per litre is a serious allegation that requires strong evidence, not merely an inference drawn from the absence of a reply," she said.
The judge also found procedural defects in the application.
However, she disagreed with the Attorney-General's Chambers' argument that the case had become academic following the introduction of a uniform diesel subsidy mechanism nationwide on July 1 this year.
She said the issues concerning APM calculations and the damages sought by the applicants remained live.
Although the application raised genuine constitutional questions, Norliza said the applicants had failed to establish an arguable case warranting a full hearing.
Azhani and Hatta filed the application on Oct 7, 2024, naming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and five others as respondents.
They sought, among others, a declaration that the government's June 9, 2024 decision to end blanket diesel subsidies and raise the retail price from RM2.15 to RM3.35 per litre was null and void.
The 56 per cent increase took effect on June 10, 2024, in Peninsular Malaysia, while Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan were exempted.

Title: Malaysian driver held with 300 cartons of untaxed cigarettes in Singapore
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A Malaysian motorist was arrested after more than 300 cartons and 200 packets of untaxed cigarettes were found hidden in various compartments of his car at Singapore's Woodlands Checkpoint.
The 29-year-old was arrested on Nov 16 after Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) selected his Malaysia-registered vehicle for enhanced checks.
ICA officers discovered the cigarettes concealed in several parts of the vehicle.
The driver and seized cigarettes were referred to the Singapore Customs for further investigation, ICA said in a statement.
The case is among several cigarette-smuggling attempts involving Malaysia-registered vehicles intercepted at Singapore's land checkpoints this year, with smugglers using increasingly elaborate concealment methods.
In previous cases, cigarettes were found hidden in modified floorboards, seats, doors, engine compartments and tyres, as well as the chassis of a Malaysia-registered
bus
.
Singapore imposes strict controls on tobacco products, with all
cigarettes
brought into the country subject to customs duty and Goods and Services Tax (GST), regardless of whether they are for personal or commercial use.
Unlike some other goods, tobacco products do not enjoy the usual GST import relief or duty-free concession granted to travellers.
Under Singapore's Customs Act and Goods and Services Tax Act, buying, selling, conveying, delivering, storing, keeping, possessing or dealing with duty-unpaid goods are serious offences.
Those convicted face fines of up to 40 times the duty and GST evaded, imprisonment of up to six years, or both.
Vehicles used in the offences and proceeds from the sale of duty-unpaid goods may also be forfeited.
The ICA has also stepped up technology-driven and intelligence-led screening at its land checkpoints, with its integrated targeting centre assessing travellers, vehicles and cargo before arrival.
Vehicles flagged as high-risk are subjected to enhanced inspections, with officers authorised to dismantle or cut open modified compartments to retrieve suspected contraband.
The latest arrest serves as another warning to motorists attempting to smuggle untaxed cigarettes across the Causeway.

Title: [UPDATED] Online fraud costs Malaysians RM7.33bil, 193,000 cases recorded
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Online fraud has cost Malaysians RM7.33 billion, with 192,869 cases recorded between 2023 and October this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 75,266 people were arrested during the same period, while 69,665 charges were filed.
He said mule accounts played a key role in enabling scam syndicates to operate, with 254,546 such accounts detected during the period.
Charges were brought against people linked to 137,699 of these mule accounts, he added.
He was responding to V. Ganabatirau (PH-Klang), who asked about the latest developments in the government's efforts to combat online fraud and mule accounts.
The question also covered the total losses suffered by the public since 2023, the amount of money successfully frozen or recovered, prosecution rates and measures to expedite the freezing of suspicious transactions before funds were transferred overseas.
Saifuddin said there were six main types of scams: telecommunications scams, e-financial crimes, love scams, e-commerce scams, non-existent loan schemes and non-existent investment schemes.
"Of these six categories, telecommunications crimes recorded the highest number of cases, with 73,043 cases involving losses of RM2.132 billion.
"E-commerce crimes ranked second in terms of the number of cases, with 50,749 cases, although losses in this category amounted to RM509 million.
"Non-existent investment schemes ranked third, with 27,863 cases. However, this category recorded the highest financial losses, amounting to RM3.4 billion."
For this year alone, between January and October, Saifuddin said 56,802 online scam cases were recorded, involving losses of RM1.56 billion and 20,842 arrests.
He said 17,985 investigation papers resulted in charges being brought against 18,369 people.
Saifuddin said the figures showed that online scam cases were on an upward trend.
"An analysis of victim profiles shows that women are more likely to fall victim to scams than men. For every 10 victims, six are women and four are men."
He said most victims were employed in the private sector.
However, students accounted for a significant proportion of those who allowed their bank accounts to be used as mule accounts.
Saifuddin said scam syndicates could not operate without mule accounts.
"That is why, two years ago, this House passed amendments to the Penal Code by introducing Sections 424A and 424D, which provide for offences involving people who allow their accounts to be used as payment instruments for criminal purposes."
Saifuddin said the police, in cooperation with Bank Negara Malaysia, would act immediately upon detecting that a victim had transferred money into a mule account linked to a scam syndicate.
He said funds were typically moved through several layers of accounts to evade detection before reaching the final recipient, who would withdraw the money.
"The entire process could take as little as five minutes, making an immediate response crucial to recovering victims' funds.
"That is why the victim's first call is critical, as it allows information to be entered into the police system for checks through the National Fraud Portal.
"Through the portal, authorities can flag or block the accounts involved. We call this critical period the 'golden hour'.
"Acting within this window gives us a chance to earmark the accounts and conduct the necessary checks. Once it is missed, tracing and recovering the money becomes much more difficult."
Saifuddin said the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) received up to 30,000 calls last month, averaging 1,000 a day.
"Before the establishment of the NSRC and the introduction of the 997 hotline, the authorities received only 300 to 400 calls daily.
"The increase in calls and complaints, which could indicate that more people are falling victim to scams, also reflects greater public awareness."
On the Semak Mule portal, which allows the public to check whether bank accounts have been flagged by police for suspected links to scams, he said it had recorded 78 million visits to date.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Caught: Express bus operator merges six departure slots into one, runs unauthorised routes
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An express bus operator was caught combining passengers booked for six different departure times onto one bus and carrying passengers on unauthorised routes at Larkin Sentral.
The violations were uncovered during a surprise inspection by Johor Road Transport Department (RTD) officers and three Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) officers at the terminal on Nov 23.
Johor RTD director Zulkarnain Yasin said the bus was initially spotted moving suspiciously around the terminal before officers stopped it for inspection.
Checks found that passengers who had bought tickets for six separate departures — 11am, 11.30am, noon, 12.30pm, 1pm and 1.30pm — had been gathered to board the same bus.
Further checks revealed that the bus was also operating beyond its authorised routes, he told the New Straits Times today.
The operator did not have approval to operate from Larkin to Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS), although some passengers had bought tickets for that destination.
It also lacked approval for northern routes despite carrying passengers bound for destinations in the north.
Zulkarnain said the operator was authorised to serve only East Coast routes.
RTD recorded statements from the passengers and driver, while the bus was detained pending further investigation.
The operator will also be summoned to assist in the investigation.
Zulkarnain said offenders could face fines of between RM1,000 and RM500,000 upon conviction under Section 22 of the Land Public Transport Act 2010.
He said RTD would continue taking action against operators who flouted regulations, warning that such practices could compromise passenger safety and disadvantage operators who complied with the rules.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor attracts 22mil visitors in 10 months, generates RM17.8bil
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor attracted 22 million visitors between January and October, marking a 7.5 per cent increase compared with the same period last year, despite regional conflicts, rising fuel prices and haze.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 4.7 million overnight visitors were recorded between January and June, comprising 3.3 million domestic tourists and 1.4 million international tourists.
Their visits generated an estimated RM17.83 billion for the state economy.
He said the figures reflected the resilience of Johor's tourism sector and put Visit Johor Year 2026 on track to meet its targets, with the year-end school holidays and festive season expected to further boost visitor arrivals.
"These positive developments give the state government confidence that Visit Johor Year 2026 is on the right track," he said during the state assembly sitting at Kota Iskandar here today.
Onn Hafiz said the state would continue upgrading its tourism products, facilities and visitor experiences to meet international standards while ensuring that local residents could still afford to enjoy the attractions.
"Bangsa Johor will always come first. Although our tourism products are being upgraded to international standards, prices for Johoreans will remain affordable, with some attractions even offering free admission," he said.
Among the state's popular attractions, Zoo Johor recorded more than 517,000 visitors between January and October, while the restored former prison, Kota Jail, received more than 800,000 visitors since the beginning of the year.
Danga Park, meanwhile, recorded more than 300,000 visitors.
Johor also plans to extend its tourism product development initiatives to all 16 local authorities, including upgrading food courts, developing mini water parks and creating community parks.
Under the Johor 2027 Budget, RM15 million has been allocated to expand the food court initiative across all 16 local authorities, while RM110 million has been set aside for mini water parks and community parks, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mersing airport plan hinges on viability study, says Onn Hafiz
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor is open to building an airport in Mersing to improve access to its 47 islands, but a comprehensive feasibility study must first establish the project's commercial viability.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the proposed airport had been identified in the Johor Structure Plan 2030 as part of efforts to improve connectivity to tourism destinations in the district.
However, the state government wants a detailed assessment of passenger demand, commercial viability, aircraft requirements, development costs, environmental impact and connectivity with Senai International Airport before proceeding with the project.
"We do not want the investment to become a white elephant after it is built," he said during the state assembly sitting at Kota Iskandar here today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Mohd Youzami Yusof (BN-Tenggaroh) on proposals to make island tourism a strategic economic driver for Mersing, including the need for an airport to improve access for tourists.
Onn Hafiz said better air connectivity was among the infrastructure requirements needed to unlock Mersing's potential as a new economic growth hub, particularly in tourism.
Under the Johor Economic Transformation Plan (JETP), the state had also identified improvements to land connectivity, including the proposed 142km East Coast Expressway Phase Four (LPT4), which will link Ulu Tiram to Mersing.
He said RM25 million had been approved under the 11th Malaysia Plan for preliminary LPT4 works, including traffic studies, engineering designs and proposed route alignment.
Mersing's 47 islands and rocky outcrops, including Pulau Rawa, Pulau Besar, Pulau Sibu, Pulau Aur and Pulau Pemanggil, offer significant potential for marine tourism.
The state government wants to position Mersing as the "Jewel of Johor" by encouraging visitors to stay longer and take part in activities such as diving and snorkelling, rather than making short visits.
Onn Hafiz said the state was working with the East Coast Economic Region Development Council (ECERDC) on a comprehensive development plan for Mersing, including a strategic masterplan study for islands within the ECER.
ECERDC was also conducting a feasibility study on a proposed breakwater in Mersing to provide sheltered waters, improve the safety of boat and ferry movements, and enhance marine transport operations.
He said the state was also developing a tourism ecosystem through Special Tourism Investment Zones (STIZ) to attract private investment in international-standard resorts, marinas, diving centres, accommodation and ecotourism products.
However, he said federal government support would be crucial to realising Mersing's tourism potential, citing the development of Langkawi in Kedah as an example.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Orkim gets sukuk rating upgrade on stronger PNB backing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has upgraded the rating of Orkim Bhd's Islamic Medium-Term Notes programme to AAis from AA-is, reflecting stronger shareholder support following Permodalan Nasional Bhd's (PNB) emergence as its majority shareholder.
The rating agency also revised the outlook to stable from positive, citing Orkim's strengthened ownership and support profile, alongside its strong standalone credit fundamentals.
"PNB, together with the unit trust funds under its management, holds a 60.2 per cent stake in Orkim following the restructuring within Yayasan Pelaburan Bumiputera and Orkim's subsequent listing.
"As at end-September, RM400 million was outstanding under the programme," it said in a statement.
MARC Ratings said Orkim's standalone credit profile continued to be supported by its leading position in domestic clean petroleum products (CPP) transportation, strong earnings visibility from long-term charters with established oil majors and high barriers to entry.
The agency also highlighted risks arising from higher borrowings to fund ongoing fleet expansion, as well as uncertainties surrounding contract renewals.
Orkim accounted for an estimated 55 per cent of Malaysian-flagged CPP tankers by vessel count as at early November 2026.
Its 21-vessel fleet includes three chemical tankers and two liquefied petroleum gas carriers, following the addition of two chemical tankers and one CPP tanker during the year.
Outstanding time charter contracts, including extension options, were valued at RM555.9 million as at end-September 2026, providing potential earnings visibility through 2032.
The company's fleet expansion and rejuvenation programme is ongoing, with three new CPP tankers scheduled for delivery from May 2027.
One vessel has secured a charter with an oil major, while charter terms for the remaining two are being finalised with existing customers.
MARC Ratings said total capital expenditure of RM600.7 million from 2026 to 2029 would be funded through term loans or sukuk, internally generated cash flows and proceeds from vessel disposals.
Orkim's stronger capital base following its initial public offering would also provide additional financial capacity to fund fleet renewal.
"Full-year contributions from the recently added vessels and the progressive delivery of newbuilds are expected to support further earnings growth over the near to medium term," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiger Woods' apparel line loses in trademark appeal
Article:
NEW YORK: A divided federal appeals court on Tuesday ordered the dismissal of a trademark lawsuit by Tiger Woods' golf apparel company, which sought approval to use its "leaping tiger" logo after another company with a similar logo objected.
Reversing a lower court ruling, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals in Pasadena, California, said courts in the state lacked jurisdiction to consider claims by Woods' Sunday Red against Tigeraire, a Louisiana company that makes cooling fans attachable to athletes' headgear.
The 2-1 majority said this was because Tigeraire, which is affiliated with the Louisiana State University Tigers, had no physical presence in California and did little business there.
Tuesday's decision does not affect Tigeraire's trademark infringement lawsuit against Sunday Red, which has been put on hold.
Lawyers for both companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Sunday Red, based in San Clemente, California, is part of TaylorMade Golf, a subsidiary of South Korean private equity firm Centroid Investment Partners.
FIFTEEN STRIPES
Sun Day Red, as Woods' brand is known, launched in February 2024, paying homage to Woods wearing red on Sundays during golf tournaments.
Its logo contains 15 stripes, one for each of Woods' major championship titles.
Shortly after Sun Day Red's launch, Tigeraire, which was launched in 2020, sent a cease-and-desist letter saying the competing logos were confusing consumers. Settlement talks failed, prompting the duelling lawsuits.
Sunday Red's lawsuit sought a declaration that it had done nothing wrong and accused Tigeraire of seeking an "unwarranted financial windfall from a larger and more successful brand". A federal judge refused to dismiss the case, and Tigeraire appealed.
IRREPARABLE HARM ASSERTED
Writing for Tuesday's majority, Circuit Judge Morgan Christen called Tigeraire's sales in California "trivial", totalling just 80 products over eight months and including only one item of apparel, a T-shirt.
She also called the cease-and-desist letter a "garden-variety" attempt to begin settlement talks, which did not support asserting jurisdiction.
Circuit Judge Milan Smith dissented. He said the majority was too quick to dismiss Sunday Red's claim that it could face irreparable harm if forced to pull products from stores and rebrand itself while Tigeraire asserted its trademark rights.
Woods, 50, launched Sun Day Red after his 27-year partnership with Nike ended.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From the CamPro engine to clean energy: How one Khazanah scholar charted Malaysia’s transition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Before venturing into renewable energy, Syed Malek Faisal Syed Mohamad was part of Proton’s powertrain team, working on the electronic systems that controlled the national carmaker’s engines.
His later work in electric mobility eventually led him to help build the renewable energy business at Gentari.
“Before I got the Khazanah-Cambridge Scholarship in 2011, I spent a lot of time in Proton.
“I graduated from King’s College London in 1997 with First Class Honours in mechatronics engineering, and right after graduation I joined Proton,” he told Malay Mail in an interview.
Where it began: Proton
Syed Malek said he had always been interested in both mechanics and electronics.
He recalled that there were few options when he was choosing his undergraduate course, with students generally opting for mechanical, electronic or electrical engineering.
“It so happened that a new course was being introduced, so I took mechatronics because I liked mechanics and I liked electronics. I was in the second batch at King’s College,” he said.
At the time, he said, Proton was moving from assembling cars to becoming a full-fledged developer that designed, developed and manufactured cars from scratch.
“So I was part of that transition with Proton. It was then the vision of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad to make it part of Malaysia’s industrial master plan, and to build local capabilities, in this case in building cars and engines,” he said.
At Proton, he developed the electronic systems that controlled the engines, which he described as the engine’s “brain”. His work involved tuning engines to meet emissions requirements while maintaining performance.
“One of the projects I worked on was the CamPro engine, which is a proud achievement for the Malaysian engineering team.
“The engine was developed from scratch and subsequently used in various Proton models. That is a testament to an excellent vision becoming reality and developing local capabilities,” he said.
Cambridge and the digital shift
After several years in the automotive industry, Syed Malek began looking towards the next stage of technological development, particularly the growing importance of electronics, computing and digitalisation.
That interest led him to pursue a master’s degree in technology policy at the University of Cambridge’s Judge Business School in 2011, supported by the Khazanah-Cambridge Trust.
He recalled that the world was then moving from industrialisation towards digitalisation, before artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres became major talking points.
“At that time there was no AI, there were no data centres,” he said.
He said the experience gave him a good foundation before he returned to Malaysia and moved into electric mobility.
Pioneering EVs with Comos
In 2014, Syed Malek joined Comos, which he described as Malaysia’s first electric vehicle (EV) start-up.
The company provided EV car-sharing services and developed a charging network at a time when electric mobility in Malaysia was still in its infancy.
He said the challenge was to establish the business while helping lay the foundations for wider EV adoption.
“Being the pioneer, there were a lot of challenges at that time. Our objective was to ensure that we could be the first mover.
“We wanted to provide a base for EV penetration here in Malaysia,” he said.
His work went beyond the business itself, extending to advocacy to secure support for the growth of the EV industry.
Building Gentari
In 2018, Syed Malek was offered the chance to join Petronas to help set up its new energy business.
The business was initially housed under the group’s corporate strategy division before becoming a standalone arm and, eventually, Gentari, which now focuses on renewable energy, clean hydrogen and green mobility.
Drawing on his EV experience, Syed Malek contributed to the early development of Gentari’s green mobility business before moving into renewable energy.
He is now head of renewable energy for Malaysia, overseeing the development, delivery and growth of the company’s renewable energy portfolio in the country.
His responsibilities include managing the business, developing strategic partnerships, overseeing project execution and expanding its presence across the utility-scale as well as commercial and industrial segments.
The road to 2050
Asked whether Malaysia was heading in the right direction with its energy transition, Syed Malek said the country had established a clear policy direction and was beginning to see demand for cleaner energy.
He pointed to the National Energy Transition Roadmap, which aims to raise renewable energy’s share of the country’s installed capacity to 70 per cent by 2050.
“Even though 2050 feels like it’s still far away, a lot of work has to start now,” he said.
He cited large-scale solar development and the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme as examples of mechanisms meant to accelerate the sector.
Demand from new industries is also becoming an important driver, particularly the growth of data centres, which consume substantial amounts of electricity. This makes access to clean energy increasingly important as Malaysia attracts more investment in the sector.
“We are doing the right thing because we need to ensure that all these data centres are not taking the full energy from the market. It has to be sustainable.
“For the renewable energy business in Malaysia, we have developed the capability, but we need to ensure that we can scale and grow bigger to support Malaysia’s bigger ambitions,” he said.
Proton’s EV ambitions realised
Looking back, Syed Malek said he was pleased to see Proton now producing EVs, a continuation of work on EV and hybrid prototypes that began more than a decade ago.
“I’m very, very happy, because the early work that we started more than 10 years ago included developing prototypes for EVs and also for hybrids,” he said.
Syed Malek’s background has also shaped his views on education and opportunity.
Originally from Pekan, Pahang, he is the eldest of 13 siblings. All 12 of his younger siblings went on to tertiary education. Nine of them earned university degrees, some of them master’s degrees, three completed diplomas, and six studied overseas.
He has since been involved in efforts to support other students pursuing similar paths.
He was among the pioneer members who set up the Khazanah Scholarship Alumni Association (KSAA), which connects former scholars with Yayasan Khazanah and gives alumni a platform to share feedback, take part in discussions and support one another.
Most recently, he was selected by Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) to mentor its scholars through a programme that helps students gain admission to universities including Cambridge, Oxford, Harvard, MIT and Yale.
For Yayasan Khazanah, its 20th anniversary marks two decades of investing in Malaysian talent. The foundation said it had developed more than 1,730 Malaysian scholars through its scholarship programmes between 2006 and 2026.

Title: Orphaned Bidayuh student from Lundu chases teaching dream at UPSI thanks to SULUNG aid
Article:
TANJONG MALIM, Nov 24  — Just a year ago, Grace Ezra Bunad, a young Bidayuh woman from the rural district of Lundu in Sarawak, considered abandoning her dream of going to university after facing financial hardship following the loss of her main source of support.
The death of her father, Bunad Jawi, in a road accident when she was 17 dealt a heavy blow to the family in Kampung Seraya Hilir, Lundu. He died shortly before she was due to sit her Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia trial examinations.
The youngest of four children said her mother made a living through small-scale farming, while her siblings worked as food outlet assistants and manual labourers.
“After finishing matriculation in Sarawak, I received an offer to further my studies at Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI). However, I was worried and nearly lost hope, thinking about the living expenses and the RM1,500 registration fee I had to come up with at short notice.
“Back then, I believed I would have to repay the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan in full, and the cost of furthering my studies was beyond what my family could afford,” she told Bernama recently.
Her hopes were revived when UPSI lecturers visited her family home in Sarawak to learn more about her family’s financial circumstances before she enrolled in September last year.
The first in her family to enter higher education, Grace Ezra was among those selected for the SULUNG 4.0 First-Generation Student Development Programme, run by the Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE).
Grace Ezra, who hopes to become a Mathematics teacher, said the SULUNG scholarship helped reduce her financial burden by covering her semester tuition fees, along with laboratory, health, and sports charges.
“I feel even more motivated knowing that I may be eligible to have my PTPTN loan converted into a scholarship if I continue to achieve excellent academic results,” said the undergraduate, who is currently in her third semester.
In addition to assistance from MOHE, Grace Ezra has also received support through several other initiatives, such as RM600 in financial aid from the Sarawak state government each semester, a RM3,000 computer voucher, book vouchers, subsidised flight tickets and the Dapur Siswa MADANI facility at her campus.
She said the SULUNG programme eased her financial difficulties while also offering emotional support through the university’s counselling unit, which tracked her academic progress.
“This support motivates me to do my best and make sure I do not disappoint those who have invested in my education. I believe that through education, I can change my family’s fortunes and provide a better life for my mother and family back home,” she said.
The SULUNG programme aims to help students from B40 families become the first in their households to pursue undergraduate studies at a public university, regardless of their chosen field.
UPSI vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Md Amin Md Taff said 206 students had received assistance under the programme since SULUNG 1.0.
“The SULUNG programme plays an important role in creating opportunities for students from low-income households to pursue higher education, especially those who are the first in their families to attend university,” he said.
Md Amin said the support not only eased tuition and study-related costs but also gave students the confidence, motivation, and ongoing support to complete their studies successfully.
“Grace Ezra Bunad’s journey demonstrates that financial and social disadvantages should not prevent young people from pursuing their dreams and creating a better future for their families through education,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Underage motorists arrested in KL surge to 114 in first 10 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Police detained 114 school students under 17 for reckless and dangerous driving in Kuala Lumpur between January and October this year, up from 69 throughout 2025.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the figure was notably higher than the 52 people detained in 2024, underscoring the need to address teenage involvement in traffic offences.
Meanwhile, he said the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department carried out 563,953 enforcement actions in the first 10 months of this year, compared with 444,594 during the same period last year.
Fadil said the actions included issuing notices and summonses, as well as seizures and arrests, under five major operations: Op Pematuhan, Op Perdagangan, Op Khas Bersepadu, Op Motosikal and Op Mabuk.
“This increase demonstrates the department’s continued commitment to intensifying enforcement efforts and ensuring that road users abide by traffic laws, he said at the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department’s rank promotion and handover of duties ceremony here today.
He said the department carried out 3,702 operations during the period, with Op Pematuhan accounting for the highest number, followed by Op Khas Bersepadu and Op Motosikal. It also recorded 990 arrests up to October this year for offences under Sections 45A, 42 and 50(3) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
However, Fadil said Kuala Lumpur recorded 67,262 road accidents between January and October this year, including 197 fatal cases, 63 cases involving serious injuries and 1,842 involving minor injuries. A further 65,160 cases involved vehicle damage.
He also said four fatal road accidents involving alcohol-related offences were recorded between January and October this year, up from three in 2025.
He called on the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department to intensify road safety awareness efforts, step up surveillance at accident-prone locations and take stronger enforcement action against traffic offences that could cause accidents. — Bernama

Title: Women’s Ministry Ministry to engage employers on wider adoption of flexible work arrangements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) is ready to negotiate with the private sector to expand Flexible Working Arrangements (FWA), particularly to help women balance career and family responsibilities.
Deputy Minister Lim Hui Ying said the ministry would discuss with stakeholders to find solutions balancing employees' interests and employers' operational needs.
"We do want (the private sector to implement FWA), but we don't want to force it. We will negotiate; if someone faces a problem, they can approach JPW (the Women's Development Department), and we will do our best to ensure it's a win-win situation," she said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She said this when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates at the committee stage for KPWKM.
Lim explained that under Sections 60P and 60Q of the Employment Act 1955, workers have the right to apply for FWA, but at the same time, employers are required to approve or reject the application in writing with reasons within 60 days from the date of the application.
"We understand that this mechanism provides clear room for negotiation, although the final decision remains subject to operational suitability and the employer's discretion.
"Therefore, KPWKM's approach focuses on strengthening a family-friendly work culture, employer awareness and ecosystem support so that the right to apply for FWA is truly translated into real opportunities for women," she said.
