Meanwhile, Lim called on more employers to provide childcare centres (TASKA) at the workplace to help ease the burden on working mothers with young children.
"I would like to take this opportunity to call on employers to provide TASKA at the workplace, as the government also provides incentives (tax deductions) for this purpose. Such facilities can give working mothers peace of mind because their children are close to their workplace," she said.
In other developments, Lim said 172,757 senior citizens nationwide received the Social Welfare Department Senior Citizens Assistance up to September 2026, comprising 72,208 men and 100,549 women, with total expenditure of RM919.8 million.
The Dewan Rakyat approved the 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates totalling RM4.355 billion allocated to KPWKM under Budget 2027 by a majority voice vote, after 24 MPs debated it. — Bernama

Title: National Laureate A. Samad Said dies, son announces
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said has died at 91, according to a social media post by his son, musician and writer Az Samad, today.
In a Facebook post, Az Samad said his father had passed away and that the family was in the process of making funeral arrangements.
“My father passed away and our family is currently arranging funeral details. Will share more information as things are confirmed,” he said.
Az also shared the announcement in Malay, saying the family was managing the burial arrangements and would provide further details once available.
A. Samad Said, widely known as Pak Samad, was one of Malaysia’s most celebrated literary figures and was conferred the National Laureate title for his contributions to the country’s literature and arts.
Born Abdul Samad Muhammad Said in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka on April 9, 1935, he is widely regarded as one of Malaysia’s most influential literary figures.
He is best known for works such as Salina (1961), Sungai Mengalir Lesu, Langit Petang and Hujan Pagi.

Title: Police to question 25 crew members over actress’ harassment claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Police have recorded statements from six individuals to assist in the investigation into allegations that an actress was a victim of sexual harassment by a male actor during the filming of a drama recently.
Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Chief SAC Sazalee Adam said that so far, those whose statements have been recorded consist of the complainant, the complainant’s fiancé who is also her personal assistant (PA), the suspect, the director, and two witnesses who are cameramen.
“Statements from at least 25 individuals comprising the filming crew will be taken in stages, according to their availability, given that they are currently working with other productions,” he said in a statement today.
He added that the investigation is still ongoing and no arrests have been made so far.
Previously, a social media post went viral on social media that the actress had alleged sexual harassment occurred during the filming of a drama. — Bernama

Title: Anwar marks four years as PM, vows to continue reforms and ease cost-of-living pressures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today marked the fourth anniversary of his swearing-in as prime minister, describing the past four years as a challenging period of rebuilding the nation while pledging to continue efforts to strengthen the economy, governance and public welfare.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he still remembered the weight of the responsibility he assumed when he took office amid economic pressures, fiscal constraints and rising living costs faced by Malaysians. He also pointed to longstanding governance weaknesses and corruption as issues that required bold reforms.
The prime minister said his goal from the first day in office was to restore the country’s strength and improve the lives of the people, acknowledging that the task had not been easy.
Anwar said the Madani Government had over the past four years laid a stronger foundation for Malaysia through efforts to improve the country’s financial position, strengthen governance, advance institutional reforms and enhance support for public welfare.
However, he said much work remained to be done, adding that the true measure of national progress was reflected in whether families enjoyed better living standards, greater income security and a brighter future for their children.
Expressing confidence in the groundwork already established, Anwar said the government would continue pursuing measures to reduce the burden on the people while creating fairer opportunities for all Malaysians.

Title: Zahid, Tok Mat and Asyraf Wajdi to meet Tuanku Muhriz on Thursday to present BN’s decision on Negeri Sembilan crisis
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 24 — Three top Barisan Nasional (BN) leaders are expected to have an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here on Thursday, Sinar Harian reported.
Citing a source, the Malay daily said the three are BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, BN deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
“The purpose of the audience is to present the party’s decision reached at a special meeting at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan last Friday night.
“As far as we have been informed, Tuanku Muhriz has consented to receive them on that date, but it is not known whether it will be cancelled at the last minute,” the source was quoted as saying.
The source added that all BN state assemblymen had been instructed by the party not to issue any statements on the ongoing crisis to avoid worsening the situation.
However, the party is working to resolve the crisis, including the issue of the Menteri Besar, the source said.
Last Friday, 24 BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen in Negeri Sembilan agreed to abide by the directives of the top leadership in resolving the political impasse.
Sinar Harian reported that the decision was made after a special meeting at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan chaired by Mohamad.
It followed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s revelation that he had never agreed to his resignation letter, dated Nov 16, being submitted to Tuanku Muhriz.
The Juasseh assemblyman also said he had only learnt of the resignation, announced by the BN leadership, through media reports.
Since then, Ismail has not made any further statements, including in response to the Negeri Sembilan palace’s call for him to prove he has the support of a majority of assemblymen.
On Sunday, the Menteri Besar’s press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said Ismail was receiving treatment at a hospital here and that his condition was improving.
As of 3pm today, the media were still awaiting an update on Ismail’s condition, including whether he had been discharged, the daily reported.

Title: ‘Busy 12 months ahead’: Hannah Yeoh jokes KL may not have enough weekends in 2027 to accommodate events
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur may not have enough weekends next year to accommodate the growing number of events and programmes planned for the capital, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh joked today.
She said the expansion of KL Festival and other creative programmes, supported by the government and private sector, would create more job opportunities while attracting domestic and international visitors.
“My only worry is we just don’t have enough weekends in 2027 to cater to all this. It’s a good problem for us in KL,” she told reporters after the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here.
Hannah said the festival’s second edition would run for 25 days, with support from the Federal Territories Ministry, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Finance Ministry, adding that she expected a bigger crowd than this year.
She said organisers were also looking to expand activities beyond the annual festival through year-round programmes, including concerts and events at public parks.
Think City, which is involved in organising the festival, said its pilot events last year generated more than 1,400 job opportunities, with the figure expected to double annually as the creative sector expands.
Hannah said the growing number of programmes would give young people more opportunities to showcase their talents and find employment.
She also cited the entertainment tax incentives announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027 in Parliament, alongside Visit Malaysia Year, as factors that would contribute to a busy year for Kuala Lumpur.
“KL Festival cannot happen without the support of the private sector. And with Visit Malaysia Year coming back a second year and together with this entertainment tax incentive that the Prime Minister has announced for Budget 2027, I believe it will be a busy 12 months in Kuala Lumpur,” she said.

Title: Hannah says KL’s heritage sites can become international attractions, points to Macron’s visit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur’s heritage landmarks have the potential to become international tourist attractions, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said, pointing to the positive public response to French President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit to the capital.
She said Macron’s walkabout through the city, including his appearance at Dataran Merdeka with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building as a backdrop, showed how Kuala Lumpur’s historic sites could help shape its appeal to international visitors.
“We could have taken him to one of our newest and tallest buildings, and the new condominium, but we took him to Dataran Merdeka with the Sultan Abdul Samad building behind it.
“I think that choice says something about how we want the world to see Kuala Lumpur. Since the inspection and the pictures went viral, we have received a lot of feedback from people. They said, what an amazing idea to take him to the Sultan Abdul Samad Building,” she said in her speech at the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here today.
Hannah said the city’s heritage should be preserved while its public spaces are made more accessible and inviting, allowing both residents and visitors to experience its history.
“When people talk about Kuala Lumpur, when people talk about the inspection of world leaders, it’s no longer just pictures in Putrajaya, but they see Pasar Seni, Medan Pasar, and all other parts of Kuala Lumpur,” she said.
She also defended the RM600 million restoration of the Sultan Abdul Samad Building, saying the work was now showing results.
Her remarks came as she announced the return of KL Festival for its third edition, which will run from May 6 to 30 next year under the theme “Bridges of Belonging”.
The festival will feature activities across downtown Kuala Lumpur, including the Dataran Merdeka Heritage Area, Masjid Jamek, Central Market and Petaling Street, with satellite events planned for Brickfields and Kampung Baru.
Hannah said initiatives such as the festival could help bring heritage spaces to life through cultural programmes and activities, while giving younger generations a greater role in shaping the city.
She said Kuala Lumpur should continue developing without losing its identity, adding that its heritage and public spaces could help give visitors reasons to return and explore.

Title: KL Festival to return next year with 25-day programme across Downtown KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — KL Festival will return to Downtown Kuala Lumpur from May 6 to 30 next year, with Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh hoping to turn the capital into a more attractive destination through cultural events and unconventional tourism offerings.
Themed “Bridges of Belonging”, the 25-day festival will feature performances, exhibitions and community activities across the city’s historic core, from the Dataran Merdeka Heritage Area to Central Market and Petaling Street, with satellite programmes in Brickfields and Kampung Baru.
“I think that what makes Kuala Lumpur important is that it gives people a reason to come back to explore,” Hannah said at the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here today.
She said Kuala Lumpur needed to explore new attractions that could appeal to different groups of visitors, including younger tourists, rather than relying solely on conventional sightseeing and shopping experiences.
Hannah recounted how she had taken her two daughters to Pasar Seni after they expressed an interest in buying Squishies, a popular collectible among young people, instead of visiting heritage attractions.
She also recalled asking a French official accompanying French President Emmanuel Macron during his visit to Kuala Lumpur last week whether he had time to explore the city.
“He said he didn’t have time because he had a meeting, but his daughter in France told him to buy something from KL for her. Guess what? A Squishy,” she said.
Hannah said the experience showed how popular culture and the interests of younger generations could create new opportunities for Kuala Lumpur’s tourism industry.
She also suggested developing themed shopping destinations, including dedicated areas for watches and perfumes, so visitors could find specialised products in one location rather than having to visit multiple places.
She said such initiatives could give tourists more reasons to return to Kuala Lumpur and explore different parts of the city.
The 2026 edition of KL Festival attracted 140,000 visitors and recorded more than 100,000 attendances, while generating more than 1,400 jobs and gigs for artists, producers, designers and crew members, according to the organisers.
Hannah said the festival’s impact should extend beyond its annual run, with the government working alongside Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Think City and the private sector to sustain cultural activities throughout the year.
“The government is behind Kuala Lumpur and we will not let Think City go it alone,” she said, urging businesses and financial institutions to support the festival through sponsorships and partnerships.
She said the creative sector could also provide more employment opportunities for young people, particularly those with skills and ideas that might otherwise have limited avenues to be showcased.
“Without events and programmes, there’ll be very little opportunity for young people with creative ideas to showcase their talent and to be hired for these kind of roles,” she said.
Think City, which organises the festival alongside DBKL with support from the Finance Ministry and the Federal Territories Department, said it had outlined a five-year roadmap to establish KL Festival as a flagship event while progressively introducing year-round activities.
Its representative said the more than 1,400 jobs and gigs generated through the 2026 edition were expected to grow, with the organisation aiming for creative-sector employment opportunities to double annually.
Among the first confirmed highlights for next year’s festival are Jogeton, a community dance celebration featuring a new segment for children, and Gema Kuala Lumpur, which will feature two all-women dikir barat performances along the River of Life.
Other programmes include Our Love Song, a musical theatre production exploring stories behind Malaysia’s national identity, including the national anthem Negaraku, and Songs of the Bulbul by British South Asian dancer Aakash Odedra.
The line-up will also feature Efectos Especiales, a free street performance from Argentina, the world premiere of HuRU-hARa: nUSaNtAra, a collaborative production involving artists from Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia and Timor-Leste, and KataRaya: KL Festival Literature Week.
Other public programmes include KL Discovery Race, a citywide treasure hunt, KL Frozen in Time, a collective photography project, KL Builds, which invites participants to recreate city landmarks using recycled materials, and KL Beat: The City Marches, a procession involving drummers and marching groups from across Kuala Lumpur.
Most festival activities will be free, while ticketed performances will be priced to keep the arts accessible. Its Pay It Forward initiative will also extend access to residents of People’s Housing Projects (PPR), schools, senior citizens’ homes and children’s homes.
More programme details, venues and ticketing information will be announced ahead of the festival.

Title: State may seek federal loan to resolve drainage problems, says Amirudin
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 24 — The Selangor state government is prepared to obtain a loan from the Federal Government if necessary to accelerate the implementation of flood mitigation projects, including resolving drainage system problems at the local authority level.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the move reflects the state government’s commitment to ensuring that flooding issues, particularly flash floods that frequently occur in urban areas, can be addressed more comprehensively.
“Given that the state government currently has no outstanding loans from the Federal Government, I believe that whether the amount is tens of millions or billions of ringgit, I think it is worth it for the state government to take out a loan to resolve these drainage problems, including those at the local authority level,” he said during the winding-up session of the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates debate at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government has also allocated RM100 million for flood mitigation purposes next year, almost double the allocation made in 2022, and it is prepared to bear additional expenses to ensure that related projects can be implemented without being overly constrained by financial limitations.
Local authorities have also been directed to allocate between 20 and 30 per cent of their respective reserves specifically for flood management, in order to strengthen urban areas’ resilience against the risks posed by changing weather patterns, he said.
“Another issue that I believe needs to be emphasised is the coordination of efforts, monitoring and communication among all agencies, so that they work together as one team to address the flooding issue,” Amirudin said.
On a related development, he said flooding in the Parit Mahang area of Ijok was caused not only by overflowing water but also by a slow drainage system due to culvert structures in front of houses, as well as incidents of broken embankments and high-tide phenomena.
He said water-pumping operations in Parit Mahang could only begin 20 days after the flooding occurred, as the high tide levels beforehand had rendered pumping efforts ineffective.
“The pumped water is channelled directly into rivers or the sea to help reduce water accumulation in the affected areas,” he said.
He also shared that the process of acquiring land used as an illegal dumping site in the Ijok area is expected to be completed around March 2027. — Bernama

Title: Federal Government remains united despite political differences, says Zahid
Article:
BALI, Nov 24 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that differences in political views and positions among parties forming the Federal Government do not affect the country’s administration.
Ahmad Zahid, also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said political maturity enabled party leaders to put aside their differences when carrying out their shared responsibility of governing the country.
“When it comes to administering the government, we set aside those differences. When discussing matters concerning national interests, we remain highly professional, and there are no disagreements,” he told Bernama here today.
He was responding to questions about the Amanah 2026 National Convention held last Sunday, where delegates passed a motion, with the support of nearly all attendees, for the party to contest the 16th General Election (GE16) without cooperating with BN.
However, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu was reported to have clarified that the resolution was merely a recommendation by the party to be submitted to the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council, with any final decision on electoral cooperation to be made at the coalition level.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, arrived in Bali on Monday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, involving a series of official engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
He is scheduled to depart for Jakarta today. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians can now renew passports through MyGov Malaysia app
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 24 — Malaysians can now renew their passports through the MyGov Malaysia app, including submitting applications, making online payments and selecting an Immigration Department office for passport collection.
In a statement today, the Digital Ministry said the enhanced MyGov Malaysia app version 2.1.4 allows the public to manage applications digitally with greater ease and speed.
According to the statement, the facility is among the key improvements introduced by GovTech Malaysia to strengthen the digitalisation of public services.
“In the initial phase, the passport collection facility is available only at the Shaftsbury Immigration Office in Putrajaya. Other collection locations will be expanded in stages to improve access and convenience for the public nationwide,” the statement said.
Besides passport renewal, the ministry said the app also enhances the MyNotifikasi function with more targeted, personalised notification delivery according to user needs.
The improvements let the public receive announcements, programme information, initiatives and important notices from ministries, departments and agencies directly through the app, so Malaysians do not miss service and initiative information relevant to them.
“MyGov  Malaysia also introduces a function to check the location of National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) under the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
“This function makes it easier for the public to identify nearby Nadi centres to access various facilities and programmes provided free of charge, including internet access, health checks and the Tuisyen Rakyat programme,” the statement said.
The ministry said the initiative also supports the expansion of digital access, improves digital literacy and strengthens learning opportunities among local communities.
The public are therefore encouraged to update the MyGov Malaysia app to the latest version via the Apple App Store, Google Play Store and Huawei AppGallery to enjoy the latest features.
“The Madani government will continue to strengthen the digital services ecosystem through cross-ministry and agency cooperation to deliver more efficient, integrated and people-centric government services, in line with Malaysia’s aspiration towards an AI Nation by 2030,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Harith Iskander’s lawyers unable to reach him, court defers bid to withdraw from Rosmah suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Lawyers representing comedian Harith Iskander in a defamation suit brought by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor have been unable to contact him despite repeated attempts, prompting the High Court today to defer their application to withdraw from the case until December 4.
High Court judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi set the new date after Harith failed to attend today’s proceedings, directing his lawyers to make further reasonable efforts to ensure he appeared in person on that date or, at the very least, provided a reasonable response, Utusan Malaysia reported.
“Until the defendant appears, I cannot allow Enclosure 15 (the application to withdraw).
“I will give one final date. Make every reasonable effort, and the court can then make an appropriate order on Enclosure 15,” she said, as reported by the national daily.
Lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo told the court that attempts to serve notice on Harith had been made through email, WhatsApp and visits to his home.
During the first attempt to serve notice at his home, the document was received by his domestic helper as Harith was not there. A subsequent letter seeking to arrange an appointment was also accepted by the helper.
“But when we returned to serve the notice on that date, neither the helper nor Harith Iskander was there. We were not allowed into the residential area,” Sangeet said.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, she said her legal team had yet to receive instructions from the comedian despite repeated attempts.
“We have made numerous attempts but have yet to obtain any instructions. So, I hope to receive a response from him,” she was quoted as saying.
Sangeet appeared alongside Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh, while Rosmah was represented by Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.
Rosmah, 74, filed the defamation suit against Harith, 60, on June 9, alleging that he had ridiculed her physical appearance during a stand-up comedy show, Harith Iskander: The Outspoken Comedy Tour, on January 17.
She alleged that Harith had displayed an image of a frightening mythical creature before showing an image of her, and had made mocking remarks about looking in the rear-view mirror while driving along a dark road.
Rosmah claimed that footage of the performance, subsequently uploaded by a TikTok user and viewed hundreds of thousands of times, had damaged her reputation and dignity as a public figure and patron of charitable organisations.
In his statement of defence filed on July 9, Harith denied that the material carried the defamatory meaning alleged by Rosmah.
He also maintained that the TikTok clip had been produced without his knowledge or consent and had been taken out of context.

Title: Perak gets RM40m for road repairs, half earmarked for Tambun and Ipoh, housing minister says
Article:
IPOH, Nov 24 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) has allocated RM40 million to Perak for road repair and resurfacing works, particularly in residential areas across the state.
Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the allocation would be disbursed soon, with all projects expected to be completed before the Hari Raya Aidilfitri celebrations.
He said the funds came from the ministry’s cost-saving measures, which had reduced wastage and improved management efficiency, generating total savings of RM67.4 million.
Of the savings, the government had decided to prioritise Perak by allocating RM40 million, including RM20 million specifically for the Tambun parliamentary constituency and surrounding areas of Ipoh, which has the highest population density in the state.
Nga said the decision to channel existing budget savings towards road resurfacing was a continuation of the ministry’s prudent spending approach, which had also been implemented earlier this year without incurring additional expenditure.
“We are not spending more, but optimising every sen to ensure that the people can feel, touch and see for themselves the achievements of a government that truly cares for them,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after the tabling of the Perak 2027 Budget by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad at the Perak Darul Ridzuan Building here today. — Bernama

Title: Masidi: Sabah awaits RM900m federal grant ahead of 2027 Budget amid oil revenue uncertainty
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 24 — The Sabah state government is preparing the 2027 Budget by reviewing all expenditure components to ensure they meet the state’s needs and priorities, in line with prudent spending principles.
Deputy Chief Minister II and State Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun said he and state officials are detailing every budget item, including basic infrastructure development.
“Careful planning is crucial to ensure large expenditures are executed responsibly without jeopardising the state’s financial management,” he told reporters after representing Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor at the 2026 Financial Assistance Handover Ceremony for Schools and Non-Islamic Religious Bodies here today.
Masidi said the additional RM900 million interim grant from the federal government is expected to strengthen the state’s financial position if channelled on time.
He said the federal government has assured the additional allocation will be received before the State Legislative Assembly sitting concludes, with payment expected at the end of this month.
Masidi explained that state revenue is influenced by fluctuations in the oil and gas sector, which contributes about 50 per cent of Sabah’s income, as well as international oil prices and currency exchange rates.
“Although international oil prices are high, the value of our ringgit is also at a high level. We sell oil in US dollars, so when the proceeds are received and converted into ringgit, the exchange rate also becomes a factor affecting our revenue.
“Therefore, the currency exchange rate is one of the factors. If the value of the ringgit is high, it does not necessarily result in increased revenue for us,” he said.
The Sabah State Legislative Assembly sitting is scheduled to begin on December 4, with the tabling of the 2027 Budget among the matters to be discussed. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan sec-gen hails Sarawak’s support for federal government after talks with Abang Johari
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 24 — A meeting between Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg in Sarawak yesterday focused, among other things, on strengthening cooperation between the federal government and the state.
Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the meeting covered several matters of mutual interest, including security, politics, the economy and public welfare.
“We agreed that political stability, economic prosperity and the well-being of the people must remain our priorities. Mutual respect, understanding and trust must continue to form the foundation of federal-Sarawak relations.
“In the context of national politics, I appreciate Sarawak’s commitment and support for the federal government’s efforts to maintain political stability and ensure continuity in the country’s administration,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said such cooperation and mutual understanding were crucial in allowing the government to focus fully on economic development agenda, implementing reforms and the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Melaka warns repeat-offending trishaw riders of licence revocation within 24 hours
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 24 — The Melaka state government is continuing its efforts to enhance the quality of trishaw services through an annual licensing programme to improve the professionalism of trishaw riders while strengthening the state’s image as a tourist destination.
State Housing, Local Government and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman said the initiative also involved improving enforcement to ensure that trishaw riders complied with the stipulated conditions and regulations.
“We need to have enforcement measures in place. The Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB) has been tasked with identifying trishaw riders who repeatedly commit offences, including revoking their licences within 24 hours.
“This concerns Melaka’s image. They must abide by the undertaking they made before being issued their licences and cannot misuse their permits to do as they please,” he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the Melaka trishaw riders briefing at Bukit Serindit here today.
Also present was MBMB Mayor Datuk Shadan Othman.
Abdul Razak said trishaw riders are among the frontline personnel in the tourism industry as they are among the first individuals to interact with tourists visiting the state.
He said 311 trishaw operators in Melaka have received new licences after attending the briefing and annual programme, which aimed to enhance their knowledge and skills to provide better services to tourists.
“This is to ensure that they gain more knowledge before going out into the field, particularly on how to warmly and courteously welcome tourists and visitors to Melaka,” he said.
Shadan said trishaw riders were also briefed on etiquette, personal appearance and service charges to ensure that they complied with the prescribed standards.
Meanwhile, he said the state government continued to provide welfare support to more than 300 trishaw operators through Hari Raya assistance and Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions amounting to nearly RM170 per person.
“The trishaw service has also been integrated into the MBMB i-Trafik application over the past year to make it easier for tourists to access the services, including contacting trishaw riders to pick them up from hotels.
“Each trishaw is also equipped with a QR code, allowing users to submit complaints directly to MBMB if they encounter any problems,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Political stability tops Saifuddin Nasution’s list of Madani government’s four-year achievements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Political stability, economic prosperity, public welfare and good governance are the four areas Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail identified as the Madani government’s key achievements over its four years in office.
Saifuddin said the administration had managed to maintain political stability, recalling the circumstances surrounding its formation on November 24, 2022.
He pointed to the parliamentary proceedings following Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s appointment as prime minister, when the government sought to establish its legitimacy through a motion of confidence in the Dewan Rakyat.
The motion was passed by a voice vote on December 19, 2022, when the government bloc comprised 148 MPs, giving it a two-thirds parliamentary majority.
“Firstly, the Madani government has succeeded in establishing political stability.
“Secondly, the Madani government has not deviated from its focus on striving for economic prosperity,” Saifuddin told a press conference after officiating at the Asia International Security Summit and Expo 2027.
He said the government had also prioritised public welfare throughout its tenure, including providing assistance to fishermen, smallholders, school students and vulnerable groups.
“Almost every segment of society has been given attention in terms of welfare,” he said.
Saifuddin identified good governance as the fourth area, saying the government had continued its efforts to address corruption, leakages and wasteful spending.
He said better financial management could allow the government to redirect savings towards helping Malaysians without necessarily introducing new taxes.
“There are times when we do not need to introduce new taxes to increase revenue.
“It is sufficient to put spending controls in place, practise prudent spending and avoid wastage, so that the money saved can be distributed to Malaysians,” he said.
Saifuddin added that the Madani administration’s approach extended beyond physical development to include efforts to develop people’s character and conscience.
“Not only should the people be developed and physical development take place, but people’s souls and consciences should also be given the opportunity to be nurtured and educated,” he said.

Title: Puchong poultry firm, four individuals charged over 6,555kg of chicken allegedly passed off as halal
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 24 — A poultry slaughterhouse, Syarikat Ayam Segar BM Sdn Bhd, and four individuals were brought before the Sessions Court here today on charges of supplying raw chicken while deceiving consumers into believing it was halal, and of abetting the offence last month.
Zafirah Karim, 36; Tanjena Akter Mollah, 35; Hosain Saddam, 34; and Abdul Rahim Ariff Ali, 34 pleaded not guilty before Judge Ainul Bashiirah Dona Don Biyajid after the charges were read to them separately.
According to the charges, the company, Zafirah and Tanjena as its directors, and Hosain as its manager, are accused of supplying 6,555 kilogrammes of slaughtered and processed chicken while making representations likely to deceive that the product was halal or fit for consumption by Muslims.
Abdul Rahim is accused of abetting Syarikat Ayam Segar BM in committing the same offence.
All the accused allegedly committed the offences on October 30 at Lot 35, Jalan Jurutera, Kampung Sri Aman Hilir, Puchong.
They are charged under subparagraph 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011, which carries a fine not exceeding RM5 million for a company and, for a second or subsequent offence, a fine not exceeding RM10 million or imprisonment of up to five years, or both upon conviction.
The directors, the manager and Abdul Rahim are charged under the same subparagraph, which carries a fine not exceeding RM1 million or imprisonment of up to three years, or both upon conviction.
For a second or subsequent offence, they face a fine not exceeding RM5 million or imprisonment of up to five years, or both, upon conviction.
Today’s proceedings were conducted by Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) deputy public prosecutor Mohd Sophian Zakaria and Selangor KPDN deputy public prosecutor Norhashimah Hashim.
Zafirah, Tanjena and Hossain were represented by lawyer Bernard Francis, while Abdul Rahim was unrepresented.
Mohd Sophian offered bail of RM40,000, with the additional conditions that all accused surrender their passports to the court and report to the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) office monthly.
Tanjena and Hossain, both foreign nationals, were not offered any bail.
“Both are Bangladeshi citizens and pose a risk of returning to their home country, which would make it difficult for the prosecution to trace them should that happen,” he said.
Bernard sought bail of RM3,500 for all his clients, citing their cooperation throughout the investigation.
Abdul Rahim, a single father supporting a nine-year-old daughter, sought the minimum sum of RM1,000.
The court then granted bail of RM35,000 each to the Malaysian accused, subject to the additional conditions of surrendering their passports to the court, reporting to the JAIS office, and not disturbing prosecution witnesses.
The two Bangladeshi nationals were denied bail, and mention was fixed for January 26 next year. — Bernama

Title: Hundreds of millions in idle research funds, missing medical prototypes: PAC flags ‘betrayal of the nation’s trust’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Hundreds of millions of ringgit in public research funds have been left idle, some for nearly two decades, alongside findings of missing medical prototypes and misused development funds, Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) revealed today, as it warned that systemic governance failures could undermine Malaysia’s technological competitiveness.
The findings were detailed in a report on the government’s Research, Development, Commercialisation and Innovation (RDCI) programme tabled in the Dewan Rakyat this morning.
PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the lack of clear refund policies and post-project assessments had left RM183.11 million in unused grant balances unreturned across 11 implementing agencies.
The Ministry of Higher Education alone has accumulated more than RM225 million in idle funds over nearly 20 years, the Masjid Tanah MP revealed.
“Leaving hundreds of millions in public funds idle, wastage caused by a lack of cooperation and communication between ministries and agencies, as well as negligence in managing assets and copyright, is a betrayal of the nation’s trust,” she told reporters in Parliament.
“The government can no longer simply approve allocations without monitoring the success and actual outcomes of a project.”
Missing medical prototypes
Months of auditing uncovered a string of costly lapses, including the disappearance of 19 units of the I-Brave Medical Prototype worth RM1.6 million at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM).
The intellectual property was also registered in the name of a former lead researcher rather than that of the government, which Mas Ermieyati described as “rather bizarre”.
“It’s bizarre, but it happened,” she said.
In an audit involving a separate ministry, the PAC found that the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) had diverted RM33.88 million towards operating expenses such as travel claims and contract staff allowances, in breach of 12th Malaysia Plan guidelines.
The sum constituted 26.9 per cent of its RDCI development allocation.
The panel also flagged what it described as siloed planning, which resulted in Mardi and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security wasting more than RM2 million on a ketum industry study that was abandoned midway due to a lack of early policy alignment with the Health Ministry.
Costly research delays
At Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), a 15-month delay in upgrading a research building plagued by mould and asbestos disrupted 27 R&D projects, forcing the government to spend an additional RM1.81 million on external laboratory rentals while exposing researchers and students to health hazards.
Mas Ermieyati warned that Malaysia’s heavy reliance on basic research without strong industry links had left local innovations uncommercialised, potentially leaving the country dependent on foreign technology in the long term.
The gap was reflected in Malaysia’s gross R&D expenditure of just 1.01 per cent of GDP against a target of 2.5 per cent, and its 34th-place ranking in the Global Innovation Index, she noted.
The panel is now urging Putrajaya to enforce mandatory grant refunds within three to six months of project completion, with budget penalties for non-compliance.
It also called for the restructuring of the central Research Management Unit (RMU), binding financial commitments from industry partners before commercialisation funds are released, and mandatory clearance from enforcement agencies before funding is allocated for studies involving controlled substances such as ketum and cannabis.

Title: Drug syndicates changing tactics, Saifuddin Nasution warns of more arrests as enforcement continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Drug syndicates may be adapting their methods and strategies, but enforcement agencies are keeping their activities under surveillance, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today, warning that more arrests would follow.
He said Malaysia’s strategic geographical position made it a key location for international drug distribution, requiring enforcement agencies to remain vigilant.
“Criminal activities may change, syndicates can come up with whatever strategies they want, but I assure you that they will not escape our radar.
“It is only a matter of how fast we get to them,” Saifuddin told a press conference after officiating at an event for the Asia International Security Summit and Expo (AISSE) 2027.
Saifuddin said drug trafficking was not the only criminal activity being monitored by enforcement agencies, which were also keeping tabs on telecommunications fraud and online scams.
He said he had received an update from the Inspector-General of Police that 13 people had been arrested, comprising seven uniformed personnel and six civilians.
“The arrests have not stopped. There will be more,” he said.
He said arrests at airports, ports and other strategic locations sent a message that the police, particularly the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department, were prepared to tackle drug trafficking.
Saifuddin said global drug trafficking patterns and the challenges faced by enforcement officers would also be discussed at the upcoming Asia International Security Summit and Expo, scheduled for January 26 to 28 next year.
He said the summit would allow enforcement personnel to gain knowledge through conferences and workshops, as well as familiarise themselves with the equipment and technologies showcased at the event.
Integrity in enforcement
Meanwhile, Saifuddin also addressed a separate case involving the arrest of a Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency (MCBA) officer over an incident at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 on November 17.
He said the case came to light after an MCBA staff member lodged a complaint against a higher-ranking officer.
“How did the case come to light? It was the MCBA personnel herself who lodged the complaint,” he said.
Saifuddin said enforcement agencies had repeatedly been reminded that protecting colleagues who violated the law would eventually have consequences for their institutions.
“There were two choices when the complaint was lodged: suppress the matter to protect the agency’s reputation or take action to uphold the law.
“We chose to act. This is a classic example,” he said.
He said the incident demonstrated that repeated reminders about integrity within enforcement agencies were not falling on deaf ears.
“I do not want to underestimate the repeated calls reminding everyone to ensure the integrity of our personnel is maintained. We should not think that these reminders go in one ear and out the other.
“This is an example of how our personnel have taken these reminders to heart, and how the information they provided led to an arrest,” he said.
Saifuddin praised the MCBA staff member for coming forward.

Title: Johor Customs intercepts two vessels in RM31.6m cigarette, diesel smuggling crackdown
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 24 — The Customs Department has crippled a cigarette and diesel smuggling syndicate, seizing goods worth a total of RM31.6 million in two separate operations in Johor waters.
Johor Customs director Aminul Izmeer Mohd Sohaimi said two vessels and 16 Myanmar crew members, aged between 25 and 53, were also detained in the operations conducted in the waters off Pengerang and Kukup.
He said in the first operation, at 11.40am on October 21, a team from the Johor Bahru Customs Enforcement Branch’s Marine Operations Unit detained a vessel in the waters off Pengerang, following intelligence shared by Indonesia’s Directorate General of Customs and Excise (DJBC).
“An inspection found 29.916 million sticks of cigarettes of various brands suspected of being non-duty-paid. The cigarettes were estimated to be worth RM5.984 million, while the duties and taxes involved were estimated at RM21 million,” he told a press conference at the Customs Marine Base in Sungai Pulai here today.
Aminul Izmeer said the vessel, which was carrying a shipment of cigarettes from Cambodia to Malaysia, and its eight crew members were detained to assist in further investigations.
In the second operation, at 10.20am on November 2, a team from the Customs Department’s Sungai Pulai Marine Unit detained an oil tanker in the waters off Kukup while it was en route from Vietnam to Malaysia.
“An inspection found that the vessel was carrying a large quantity of liquid believed to be diesel, suspected of not having been cleared by Customs. The vessel’s captain also failed to produce any valid travel documents,” he said.
He said 569,000 litres of diesel, worth RM1.395 million, involving duties and taxes amounting to RM227,000, were seized, while the vessel and its eight crew members were detained to assist in further investigations.
He said both vessels were registered overseas, but further details were still being investigated.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 135(1)(e) of the Customs Act 1967, which provides for a fine or imprisonment of not less than six months and not more than five years, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia eyes Indonesia’s village rating model under new rural development partnership
Article:
BALI, Nov 24 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish a Joint Working Group (JWG) to strengthen cooperation in rural development, including through the exchange of best practices in village management in both countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is currently on a working visit to Indonesia, said Malaysia could benefit from Indonesia’s experience specifically its more structured village rating system to improve data collection and the effectiveness of rural development programme implementation.
He noted that Indonesia classifies its approximately 75,000 villages into four categories compared to about 15,000 villages in Malaysia as developed, developing, lagging, and severely lagging.
He added that this rating system could serve as a reference for developing an index or set of standards to measure the level of village development, thereby assisting the government in planning development programmes more effectively.
“We also aim to have an index or standard for ranking these villages something we have already implemented though their system is more structured.
“We can leverage this to further improve data collection and determine how such data can be utilised for the implementation of government programmes,” he told Bernama during a visit to Tegallalang Village here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, arrived in Bali on Monday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, which includes a series of engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
He began today’s agenda with a bilateral meeting with Indonesia’s Deputy Minister of Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions, Ahmad Riza Patria in which both sides agreed to establish a Joint Working Group (JWG) following the visit to Tegallalang Village and he is scheduled to continue his visit to Mas Village.
Furthermore, he noted that another approach worth studying is the Indonesian government’s development of ecotourism for instance, by transforming terraced rice padi fields as tourist attractions where the benefits are shared not only by the farmers but by the entire village community.
He added that Indonesia also utilises village-owned enterprises known as *Badan Usaha Milik Desa* (BUMDes), which engage in economic activities such as the production of handicrafts for the export market.
He also cited rural development programmes such as Desa Kirana and Desa Lestari in Malaysia, as well as Indonesia’s Desa Mandiri (Independent Village) programmes which are similar in nature but they differ in their implementation.
“By fostering this integration, they can learn from us, and we can learn from them, allowing us to further improve upon what has already been established,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid is scheduled to depart for Jakarta on Tuesday afternoon to attend the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM) and the 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER) in Tangerang, Banten.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Riza said his side plans to conduct a reciprocal visit to Malaysia in the near future to study the country’s approach to village management and development.
“There is much we can learn specifically regarding the management of villages in Malaysia which will serve as a valuable experience for us,” he told Bernama.
He also highlighted the need for both nations to collaborate on village development in the Malaysia-Indonesia border regions, not only to strengthen communication ties but also in terms of rural development policy. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast across much of Malaysia until 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several states and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan until 5pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect the whole of Perlis.
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Baling, Sik and Kulim in Kedah; Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar and Kinta in Perak; Jeli, Gua Musang and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Pekan, Jerantut and Rompin in Pahang; Kuala Langat, Sepang, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Hulu Langat, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; as well as Mersing and Kota Tinggi in Johor.
In Sarawak and Sabah, the affected areas are Mukah (Mukah, Matu, Dalat and Daro), Sibu (Selangau), Bintulu, Miri (Subis, Miri and Marudi), Kuching, Samarahan (Samarahan and Asajaya), Limbang, Sri Aman (Pantu), Serian and Kapit (Song, Bukit Mabong and Kapit); and Kudat, Sandakan, Tawau, the Interior (Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu and Sipitang) and the West Coast (Ranau and Papar). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia must bolster cyber defences as attacks threaten to paralyse government systems, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Cyberattacks targeting critical government systems could paralyse national institutions, underscoring the need for Malaysia to strengthen its security capabilities and preparedness, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
He said cyberattacks had emerged as a growing security threat, with incidents in several countries demonstrating how government systems, including taxation, electoral and police databases, could become targets.
“Over the past few months, the trend has led to the prime minister making a statement in Parliament.
“Coincidentally, that week, there were widespread cyberattacks in Belgium involving its taxation system, in the United States involving its Election Commission system, and in Japan involving police information,” Saifuddin told reporters at an event for the Asia International Security Summit and Expo (AISSE) 2027 here.
The home minister said the attacks had prompted Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to instruct the National Security Council director-general to brief all MPs on cyber threats, a briefing that had since taken place.
He warned that such attacks could paralyse government systems unless they were addressed swiftly, professionally and with adequate technological capabilities.
“Imagine if information about national security or population data were attacked, or if the Election Commission’s data or police information were compromised.
“These are attacks against institutions,” he said.
Saifuddin said Malaysia could not afford to rely solely on existing regulations, government committees and institutional structures to address evolving threats.
He stressed that public awareness was equally important, given the potential for cyberattacks to disrupt the functioning of an entire country.
“We have the National Security Council. We have government committees dealing with cyberattacks. We have all these things.
“It is not a question of rules and regulations, or the systems and resources we already have.
“It is about creating a high level of awareness among the people that today’s security threats can come in the form of cyberattacks capable of paralysing a country’s institutions,” he said.
He added that the Home Ministry was giving particular attention to strengthening national security and enforcement capabilities.
Saifuddin said the upcoming AISSE would bring together government agencies, security organisations, industry players and international strategic partners.
The three-day event, scheduled for January 26 to 28 next year, will carry the theme “Future Proofing Nations: Security Empowered by AI”.
Saifuddin said Malaysia was not seeking to compete with major powers such as the United States and China in developing artificial intelligence (AI), given the billions of US dollars they had invested in the field.
Instead, the country would focus on applying AI to address practical security challenges, including border management and threats on land, at sea and in the air.
“We are focusing on the application of AI to manage or find solutions to problems.
“In the context of our management, it is about how AI applications can be used to benefit the country, particularly in the security sector, including border security management and threats on land, at sea and in the air,” he said.
He said the summit would allow experts, security agencies and industry players to exchange ideas and explore how AI-powered technologies could help address enforcement and security challenges.
All 11 agencies under the Home Ministry were expected to participate in the event, he added.
Discussions with international experts and industry representatives would also help the ministry review its policies to ensure they kept pace with evolving security threats.
“The policies cannot be rigid or static. They must be dynamic and move with the times,” he said.

Title: Malaysia plans to make Year One entry compulsory for six-year-olds from 2029, Education D-G says
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 24 — Malaysia plans to lower the compulsory primary school entry age from seven to six in 2029, following a two-year period during which parents will have the option of enrolling their children in Year One a year earlier.
Education director-general Datuk Mohd Azam Ahmad said the transition would give the Education Ministry time to prepare schools, adapt the curriculum and equip teachers to cater to younger pupils, the New Straits Times reported.
The move, which will require amendments to the Education Act 1996, follows a mixed initial response from parents, although the ministry says interest in early enrolment has since grown.
As of September 30, the ministry had received 73,498 applications for Year One places from six-year-olds for the 2027 academic year, accounting for nearly 15 per cent of the 491,649 applications received.
Speaking at a media briefing, Azam said preparations had begun this year to ensure the policy could be implemented and sustained.
“We do not want an initiative that has been planned to eventually stall before it is fully implemented,” he said.
Azam expressed confidence in the ministry’s ability to accommodate the additional pupils, saying additional classrooms could be built within three months using the Industrialised Building System, depending on demand.
Other measures could include operating schools in two sessions and directing pupils to schools with lower enrolment.
The curriculum, he said, already accounted for the learning needs of six-year-olds, while teacher training would be adapted accordingly.
Azam said the policy was intended not simply to bring forward the start of formal schooling but to respond to broader societal and technological changes while ensuring more equitable access to education.
“Even at a young age, children now have access to a wide range of knowledge and information. Their potential must therefore be harnessed,” he said.
Azam said some parents had also submitted appeals for early enrolment after seeing the ministry’s preparations.
Such appeals would be considered based on the readiness of classrooms and the availability of places at individual schools.
The ministry has also drawn up preliminary estimates of the additional classrooms, textbooks and teachers that would be needed should applications rise in 2028.

Title: Pardons Board minutes declassified to help AG prepare affidavit, now public documents, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The minutes of the Pardons Board meeting were declassified to help the Attorney General (AG) prepare an affidavit in a judicial review brought by the Bar Council, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
“The first reason for declassifying the minutes of the Malaysian Pardons Board was to help the AG prepare an affidavit to face the case brought by the Bar Council at the court level for the purpose of a judicial review.
“Then, the prime minister has urged that if there are any elements suggesting confidential information had been leaked, the police initiate an investigation,” Saifuddin told reporters after the launch of the Asia International Security Summit and Expo 2027.
He said the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), who stood beside him at the press conference, was ready to mobilise all resources to identify those responsible.
“The documents had already been declassified. Declassified from where? From the Official Secrets Act.
“The moment we declassify them and remove them from the Official Secrets Act, they become public documents,” he said.
The minister said he would leave the matter to the IGP.
“I was standing behind the prime minister when he answered the question.
“When he gave that answer, I could already picture the face of the IGP,” he said.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim dismissed accusations in Parliament that the government was responsible for leaking the minutes of the Pardons Board meeting concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Anwar stressed that neither the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department nor the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) had circulated the minutes.
He added that the Home Ministry should investigate how the document came to be circulated prematurely and identify those responsible.

Title: Five-month-old baby hurt in monkey attack at Sungai Buloh house
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — A five-month-old baby boy sustained facial injuries after a wild monkey attacked him at his home in Kampung Paya Jaras Tengah, Sungai Buloh, last Sunday.
Sungai Buloh police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police received a report regarding the incident at 11.44 pm on the same day.
He said the incident occurred at 8.18 pm when the victim’s 18-year-old mother was in the kitchen and the baby was sleeping in a cradle in the living room.
“The victim’s mother heard screams before discovering a monkey near the baby.
“The monkey likely entered the house through an open window and fled the same way,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Hafiz said the victim, the second child of the woman, was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for  treatment.
He said the police report has been classified as Refer to Other Agency (ROA) to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) Peninsular Malaysia.
He advised the public to stay vigilant and prioritise safety to prevent similar incidents.
In addition, the public should avoid spreading unverified information about this incident to prevent confusion, he said.
Anyone with information related to the case may contact investigating officer Sgt Maj Azmir Azriezal Ramli at 019-5665870 or the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters (IPD) operations room at 03-61561222, he added. — Bernama
